prompt: We need a Terraform template that creates a set of Amazon S3 buckets for testing purposes, where every bucket name is dynamically prefixed with the current AWS account ID. Specifically, the template must provision one standalone bucket with the suffix "bucket2", two count-based buckets with the suffixes "bucket3" and "bucket4", and four additional buckets defined via local map and list collections using the suffixes "bucket101", "bucket102", "bucket103", and "bucket104". Every bucket must block all public access and use default SSE-KMS encryption with a single shared customer-managed KMS key created by the template.

We need a Terraform template that creates a versatile AWS KMS module capable of managing customer master keys, replica keys, imported external key material, aliases, and key grants for centralized encryption management. The template must support mutually exclusive creation flags to provision either a standard customer-managed KMS key with AWS-provided key material, an external KMS key with base64 key material, a standard multi-region replica key referencing a primary key ARN, or a replica external key with custom key material and primary external key ARN. Key policy generation must be dynamically constructed based on role inputs, supporting a default root policy, key owners, administrators, standard key users, service users, EC2 Auto Scaling roles, specific cryptographic operation users (symmetric, HMAC, asymmetric public encryption, asymmetric sign/verify), Route 53 DNSSEC signing service permissions, and custom policy statements or override documents. Finally, the module should provision KMS aliases using exact names or name prefixes, as well as KMS grants with grantee principals, allowed operations, retiring principals, and optional encryption context constraint subsets.

We need a Terraform template that creates an Amazon SNS topic and subscription architecture supporting server-side encryption and delivery feedback logging. The template must support optional creation of a dedicated KMS key with a 7-day key deletion window, key rotation enabled, and an automated key policy permitting CloudWatch Logs service encryption and account root administration, while automatically assigning an alias prefixed with "alias/sns/" derived from the topic name. KMS encryption for the SNS topic must dynamically select between the newly created KMS key ARN, an explicitly provided KMS master key ARN, or fallback to "alias/aws/sns" depending on input configurations. Additionally, the setup must support optional creation of an SNS topic policy using a custom JSON string, feedback role ARNs and sample rates for Application, HTTP, Lambda, SQS, and Firehose endpoints, FIFO topic settings with content-based deduplication, and a dynamic map of subscriptions supporting flexible endpoint, protocol, auto-confirmation, raw message delivery, filter policy, and redrive policy parameters.

We need a Terraform template that creates a comprehensive IAM access management infrastructure to organize development team permissions and EC2 instance access. The configuration must feature independent boolean creation toggles for an IAM developer group, an IAM read-only and S3 read/write access policy, the group policy attachment, IAM users, an EC2 console screenshot policy, the user policy attachments, group membership associations, and an EC2 instance role. Default settings must configure an IAM group named "developers", a list of default users including "jack" and "jones" tagged with "user_created_by" set to "terraform", an IAM policy named "iam_read_only_and_s3_full_access" containing default statements for IAM read actions and S3 object read/write access attached to the group, an IAM policy named "ec2_get_console_screenshot" granting EC2 console screenshot permissions attached directly to each created user, user membership in the developers group, and an EC2 assume role named "instance_role" attached to the AWS-managed "IAMReadOnlyAccess" policy ARN.

We need a Terraform template that creates a multi-cluster Kubernetes networking foundation to support cross-cluster communication testing across three availability zones. The stack must deploy a VPC using the official AWS VPC module with a CIDR block of "10.0.0.0/16", configured with a single NAT gateway to service three private subnets calculated using a prefix length extension of 4 (e.g., /20 subnets at netnums 0, 1, 2) and three public subnets calculated using a prefix length extension of 8 starting at offset 48 (e.g., /24 subnets at netnums 48, 49, 50). The public subnets must be tagged with "kubernetes.io/role/elb" set to 1, the private subnets tagged with "kubernetes.io/role/internal-elb" set to 1, and all resources tagged with Blueprint matching the VPC name and GithubRepo set to "github.com/aws-ia/terraform-aws-eks-blueprints". Additionally, provision two dedicated security groups within the VPC, named "cluster1_additional_sg" and "cluster2_additional_sg", where each security group has ingress and egress rules allowing all protocols only to and from the other cluster's security group, enabling reciprocal cross-cluster communication between cluster1 and cluster2.

We need a Terraform template that creates a comprehensive, highly configurable AWS Cognito User Pool stack to manage user authentication, client app integration, and custom domain routing. The template must declare default variables for the pool name ("Pool name"), alias attributes (["email", "phone_number"]), auto-verified attributes (defaulting to empty), email verification message ("Some message {####}"), email verification subject ("Some subject"), MFA configuration ("OPTIONAL"), SMS authentication message ("SMS authentication message {####}"), SMS verification message ("SMS verification message {####}"), verification message template by link, SMS configuration map (with empty external ID and SNS caller ARN), recovery mechanisms (verified_email with priority 2, verified_phone_number with priority 1), invite message templates, admin create user only flag (defaulting to false), software token MFA enabling (defaulting to true), case sensitivity option (defaulting to null), dynamic device configuration parameters (defaulting to null), optional Lambda trigger configuration map (defaulting to empty), and custom schema definitions (defaulting to a required, mutable string email attribute). The module must conditionally provision SMS configuration when both external ID and SNS caller ARN are non-empty, software token MFA, username case sensitivity, device configuration, custom email sender Lambda triggers, and handle schema definitions with or without min/max string constraints while ignoring changes to estimated_number_of_users. Additionally, support dynamic iteration over a list of client app names defaulting to empty, creating User Pool Clients configured with generate_secret defaulting to false, token validities (access token: 120, ID token: 120, refresh token: 7) paired with token_validity_units (access_token: "minutes", id_token: "minutes", refresh_token: "days"), allowed OAuth user pool client flag (defaulting to false), token revocation (defaulting to true), explicit auth flows (["ALLOW_REFRESH_TOKEN_AUTH", "ALLOW_USER_PASSWORD_AUTH", "ALLOW_USER_SRP_AUTH"]), prevent_user_existence_errors ("LEGACY"), and configurable read/write attributes, callback URLs, logout URLs, OAuth flows, OAuth scopes, and supported identity providers. Furthermore, conditionally create a Cognito user group when a group name variable is non-empty (accepting precedence defaulting to 0 and an optional IAM role ARN), a Cognito User Pool domain when a domain string variable is non-empty (accepting an optional ACM certificate ARN), and an alias Route 53 A-record targeting the domain CloudFront distribution ARN (using fixed CloudFront zone ID "Z2FDTNDATAQYW2") when a create_route53_record boolean flag defaulting to false is set to true alongside a provided Route 53 zone ID.

We need a Terraform template that creates a custom three-subnet VPC network layout with public and private routing capabilities to support general application deployment testing. The configuration must declare variables for a VPC CIDR block defaulting to "10.0.0.0/16", VPC name defaulting to "DevOps-Project-VPC", Internet Gateway name defaulting to "devops-project-igw", route table name defaulting to "DevOps-project-RT", public subnet identifier name defaulting to "subnet_a", NAT gateway name defaulting to "DevOps-NAT-GW", and a public IPv4 pool name defaulting to "amazon". It must define three subnets with configurable CIDR blocks, availability zones, public IP mapping flags, and name tags, defaulting as follows: Subnet A with CIDR "10.0.1.0/24", the first availability zone in the region, and name "Subnet-A-Public"; Subnet B with CIDR "10.0.2.0/24", the second availability zone in the region, and name "Subnet-B-Private"; and Subnet C with CIDR "10.0.3.0/24", a third, distinct availability zone in the region, and name "Subnet-C-Private", with automatic public IP assignment on launch disabled by default for all three subnets. The VPC must enable DNS support and hostnames, attach the tagged Internet Gateway, and include a route table tagged with the route table name that contains a default route to the internet via the Internet Gateway, associated explicitly only with Subnet A. Additionally, provision a VPC-scoped Elastic IP drawn from the configured public IPv4 pool to deploy a NAT gateway tagged with the NAT gateway name inside Subnet B with an explicit dependency on the Internet Gateway, alongside a custom security group tagged "DefaultSecurityGroup" within the VPC that permits outbound egress traffic only within the VPC CIDR, and output the NAT gateway's public IP.

We need a Terraform template that creates a complete AWS Backup solution with automated multi-tiered backup plans, resource selection rules, IAM permissions, and optional notification configurations for enterprise backup management. The infrastructure must provision a KMS key with key rotation enabled to encrypt an AWS Backup vault whose name defaults to "my-backup-vault", accepting optional resource tags. It must set up an IAM role assumed by backup.amazonaws.com attached to the managed AWSBackupServiceRolePolicyForBackup policy to execute backup operations. The template must construct three distinct backup plans named after the vault with suffixes "-daily", "-weekly", and "-monthly", each containing an advanced backup setting enabling WindowsVSS for EC2 resources, along with corresponding backup selections named "daily_backup_selection", "weekly_backup_selection", and "monthly_backup_selection" targeting all resources ("*") matching string-like tag conditions on a configurable tag key defaulting to "backup" for values "daily", "weekly", and "monthly", respectively. The daily backup plan rule ("daily_backup_rule") must use a default schedule of "cron(0 12 ? * * *)", a lifecycle deletion threshold of 7 days, and an optional continuous backup flag defaulting to false; the weekly backup plan rule ("weekly_backup_rule") must use a default schedule of "cron(0 12 ? * 1 *)" and a lifecycle deletion threshold of 31 days; and the monthly backup plan rule ("monthly_backup_rule") must use a default schedule of "cron(0 12 1 * ? *)" and a lifecycle deletion threshold of 366 days. Finally, the template must conditionally provision backup vault notifications controlled by a boolean flag defaulting to false, sending alerts to a specified SNS topic ARN for a configurable event list defaulting to BACKUP_JOB_FAILED, RESTORE_JOB_FAILED, COPY_JOB_FAILED, S3_BACKUP_OBJECT_FAILED, and S3_RESTORE_OBJECT_FAILED.

We need a Terraform template that creates a multi-AZ highly available VPC network architecture with redundant NAT gateways for testing environment deployments. The template must configure input variables for an AWS region defaulting to "us-east-1", an environment tag ("env") defaulting to "test", a VPC CIDR defaulting to "10.0.0.0/16", public subnet CIDRs defaulting to ["10.0.10.0/24", "10.0.11.0/24"], private subnet CIDRs defaulting to ["10.0.20.0/24", "10.0.21.0/24"], and common tags containing an Owner of "Valerii Vasianovych" and Project of "Terraform AWS". The VPC must be named using the environment tag value followed by "-vpc", carry a custom tag recording the current AWS region merged with the common tags, and attach an Internet Gateway named using the environment tag value followed by "-igw". Public subnets must not map public IPs on launch, be spread across the available availability zones in the region, be named using the environment tag value followed by "-public-subnet-" and a sequential index, and route default internet traffic ("0.0.0.0/0") through a single shared public route table named using the environment tag value followed by "-route-public-subnets". Additionally, the template must provision dedicated Elastic IPs and NAT Gateways matching the count of private subnets, placed inside the corresponding public subnets and named using the environment tag value followed by "-nat-eip-" and "-nat-gw-" plus a sequential index, paired with separate private route tables named using the environment tag value followed by "-route-private-subnets-" plus a sequential index that route outbound traffic to their respective NAT Gateway, for private subnets named using the environment tag value followed by "-private-subnet-" plus a sequential index.

We need a Terraform template that creates a conditionally deployed Amazon EKS cluster along with its required IAM service role to host containerized workloads. The infrastructure must set up an IAM role named "eks-cluster" assumed by the "eks.amazonaws.com" service principal, attached to both the managed AmazonEKSClusterPolicy and AmazonEKSVPCResourceController policies. The EKS cluster resource itself must be conditionally created based on a boolean variable named create_eks defaulting to false, configured with configurable variables for cluster_name defaulting to an empty string, cluster_version defaulting to null, and authentication_mode defaulting to "API_AND_CONFIG_MAP" while explicitly setting bootstrap_cluster_creator_admin_permissions to true. For network placement, the cluster VPC configuration must dynamically evaluate subnet options by selecting control_plane_subnet_ids if populated, otherwise falling back to subnet_ids, with both list variables defaulting to empty. Finally, enforce explicit dependencies to ensure the cluster waits for both IAM role policy attachments before creation and releases them only after cluster destruction.

We need a Terraform template that creates environment-specific IAM service accounts and access credentials for CI/CD integration across development, testing, and production environments. The stack must deploy three IAM users named "DevUser-rwwise.dev", "TestUser-rwwise.dev", and "ProdUser-rwwise.dev", each configured under the path "/system/" and tagged with a Name of "rwwise.dev Infrastructure Setup", Repository of "https://github.com/zangrum/setup.inf.rwwise.dev", and dynamic account and user IDs fetched from the current AWS caller identity context. Every user must have an active IAM access key generated alongside a dedicated inline user policy named "dev_cicd_user_policy", "test_cicd_user_policy", and "prod_cicd_user_policy", respectively. The policy documents attached to all three users must contain identical statements granting: read-only/list access to CodeBuild, CodeCommit, CloudWatch metrics, EventBridge rules/targets, and CloudWatch logs across all resources; CodeStar Connections connection lookup permissions for "arn:aws:codestar-connections:*:*:connection/*" under statement ID "CodeStarConnectionsUserAccess"; CodeStar Notifications rule description for all resources constrained by a StringLike condition on "codestar-notifications:NotificationsForResource" matching "arn:aws:codebuild:*" under statement ID "CodeStarNotificationsPowerUserAccess"; and general listing access for CodeStar Notification rules, event types, and targets under statement ID "CodeStarNotificationsListAccess".

We need a Terraform template that creates a customizable Amazon EventBridge event processing module to route system events to target services. The module must accept dynamic inputs for an optional name variable defaulting to null (which uses a default naming module to fall back to "default" if null or empty), a tags map defaulting to empty, a bus configuration map defaulting to empty (which validates non-null input and supports an optional event_source_name parameter defaulting to null), a rules list defaulting to empty (which validates non-null input), and a targets list defaulting to empty (which validates non-null input). A custom EventBridge bus named after the module name must be conditionally created only when the name does not equal "default". EventBridge rules defined in the rules list must be generated using each rule's name key, inheriting optional parameters for description, event_pattern, and schedule_expression (defaulting to null), while attaching to the custom event bus if created. Additionally, provision an IAM role named after the module name with an "-invoke" suffix assumed by the EventBridge service principal ("events.<dns_suffix>") with an inline policy named after the module name with an "-invoke-targets" suffix permitting "lambda:InvokeFunction" and "states:StartExecution" across all resources. Finally, event targets defined in the targets list must be generated with explicit dependencies on the rules, linking each target's specified rule and ARN, attaching to the custom event bus if created, and dynamically assigning the created IAM role ARN only if the target ARN contains "stateMachine".

We need a Terraform template that creates a self-contained AWS Backup module with dynamic resource naming, customizable lifecycle rules, and IAM service permissions for automated backup orchestration. The module must provision an IAM role prefixed with "aws-backup-" assumed by the "backup.amazonaws.com" service principal attached to the managed AWSBackupServiceRolePolicyForBackup policy. The backup vault must be named using the prefix "vault-" followed by a name value and the suffix "-backup", accept an optional KMS key ARN, tag resources with a Job tag built from the name value followed by "-backup", and conditionally attach an access policy document when a vault policy variable is non-empty. The backup plan must be named using the prefix "plan-" followed by the name value and the suffix "-backup", tagged with the same Job tag pattern, and contain a rule named using the prefix "rule-" followed by the name value and the suffix "-backup" targeting the vault, with configurable schedule parameters (start window defaulting to 60 minutes, completion window defaulting to 120 minutes), recovery point tags using the same Job tag pattern, lifecycle transitions (cold storage after 30 days, deletion after 120 days), and dynamic copy actions mapped from a destination vault map variable defaulting to empty. The backup selection must be named using the prefix "selection-" followed by the name value and the suffix "-backup", linked to the created IAM role and plan, containing an empty condition block, and filtering resources via tag selection with operation type defaulting to "STRINGEQUALS", key defaulting to "Backup", and value defaulting to "true". Finally, the vault must conditionally configure event notifications when an SNS topic ARN variable is non-empty, defaulting subscribed events to "BACKUP_JOB_FAILED" and "COPY_JOB_FAILED".

We need a Terraform template that creates a custom cross-account IAM role and policy integration to grant third-party security auditing platform access. The infrastructure must set up an IAM role whose name is configurable via a rolename variable defaulting to "WizAccess-Role", configured with an assume role policy that allows cross-account access to an AWS principal specified by a remote-arn variable defaulting to "arn:aws:iam::830522659852:role/prod-us43-AssumeRoleDelegator", constrained by a StringEquals condition on "sts:ExternalId" matching an external-id variable defaulting to "fc959d31-537c-4108-8b87-9af9e0c9b8d2". Attach the AWS-managed ViewOnlyAccess and SecurityAudit policies to the role, alongside an inline role policy named "WizCustomPolicy" that grants explicit permissions across seven distinct policy statements: read-only access across multiple services (ACM, API Gateway, Backup, CloudTrail, CodeBuild, Cognito Identity, Connect, DynamoDB, EC2, ECR, EKS, EFS, EMR, SSM, Glacier, Glue, Health, Kafka, Kendra, Kinesis Analytics/Video, KMS, Lambda, Logs, Amazon Profiles, S3, SES, VoiceID, WAFv2, Wisdom, Macie2, Identity Store, SSO Directory, CloudWatch metrics) on all resources; EBS snapshot creation and metadata retrieval actions (CopySnapshot, CreateSnapshot, GetEbsEncryptionByDefault, DescribeSnapshots) on all resources; tag creation on EC2 snapshots in any region; KMS alias creation on the "wizKey" alias and on any KMS key in any region and account; KMS key policy actions (GetKeyPolicy, PutKeyPolicy) on all resources matching a resource tag condition of "aws:ResourceTag/wiz" equal to "auto-gen-cmk"; snapshot deletion and modification on all resources matching an EC2 resource tag condition of "ec2:ResourceTag/wiz" equal to "auto-gen-snapshot"; and an explicit Deny statement under statement ID "WizAccessS3" for "s3:GetObject" across all resources.

We need a Terraform template that creates a flexible AWS Transit Gateway module to support central hub-and-spoke network routing and cross-account RAM sharing. The template must include a create boolean variable defaulting to true to toggle between provisioning a new Transit Gateway or looking up an existing one (via an id variable defaulting to null or filtering by a name tag defaulting to null). When creating the Transit Gateway, both default route table association and default route table propagation must be explicitly disabled, while allowing configuration of BGP ASN defaulting to 65200, auto_accept_shared_attachments, dns_support, vpn_ecmp_support, and transit_gateway_cidr_blocks (which validates that all entries are valid IPv4 or IPv6 CIDRs). Additionally, process a map of route_tables where each item conditionally creates a new Transit Gateway route table or looks up an existing one using a transit-gateway-id filter paired with a tag:Name filter, assigning route table tags from merged global tags, local_tags, and a fallback name tag equal to the table name or the main resource name. Finally, if a shared_principals map variable contains entries, provision an AWS RAM resource share that permits external principals, defaulting its share name to an explicit ram_resource_share_name variable or the main resource name, associate the Transit Gateway to the share, and attach each principal specified in the map.

We need a Terraform template that creates a tiered AWS Backup architecture to manage automated snapshot retention across Bronze, Silver, Gold, and Premium service levels. The template must provision a shared KMS key with a 10-day deletion window and key rotation enabled, alongside an IAM role named "Bronze_Backup_Role" assumed by backup.amazonaws.com attached to the AWSBackupServiceRolePolicyForBackup and AWSBackupServiceRolePolicyForRestores managed policies. Each service tier must feature a dedicated backup vault encrypted with the shared KMS key, a corresponding backup plan, and a resource assignment filtering resources where the tag key "Backup" equals the respective tier name in lowercase (for example "bronze") using a STRINGEQUALS comparison. Specifically, the Bronze tier vault ("Bronze_Backup_Vault") must pair with the "Bronze_Backup" plan containing a weekly rule ("Bronze_Backup_Weekly") scheduled at "cron(0 0 ? * FRI *)" retaining backups for 10 days, assigned via "Bronze_Resource_Assignment". The Silver tier vault ("Silver_Backup_Vault") must pair with the "Silver_Backup_Plan" containing a daily rule ("Silver_Backup_Daily") scheduled at "cron(0 5 ? * * *)" retaining backups for 7 days, assigned via "Silver_Backup_resource". The Gold tier vault ("Gold_Backup_Vault") must pair with the "Gold_Backup" plan containing three rules: a daily rule ("Gold_Daily_Backup_Rule") at "cron(0 0 * * ? *)" retaining for 31 days, a monthly rule ("Gold_Monthly_Backup_Rule") at "cron(0 0 1 1/1 ? *)" retaining for 365 days, and a yearly rule ("Gold_Yearly_Backup_Rule") at "cron(0 0 31 12 ? *)" retaining for 2555 days, assigned via "Gold_Backup_Select". Finally, the Premium tier vault ("Premium") must pair with the "Premium" plan containing four rules: a 4-hour rule ("Premium_Daily_4Hour_Backup") at "cron(0 0/4 ? * * *)" retaining for 1 day, a daily rule ("Premium_Daily_Backup") at "cron(0 0 * * ? *)" retaining for 31 days, a monthly rule ("Premium_Monthly") at "cron(0 0 1 1/1 ? *)" transitioning to cold storage after 15 days and deleting after 365 days, and a yearly rule ("Premium_Yearly") at "cron(0 0 31 12 ? *)" transitioning to cold storage after 15 days and deleting after 2555 days, assigned via "Premium".

We need a Terraform template that creates a simple two-subnet VPC networking environment named "development-be-vpc" for backend development testing in us-east-1. The VPC should use the CIDR block "10.0.0.0/16" (configurable, as are the subnet CIDRs) with DNS hostnames and DNS support enabled, and contain a public subnet named "development-be-public-subnet" with CIDR "10.0.1.0/24" in the first availability zone that does not auto-assign public IPs on launch, and a private subnet named "development-be-private-subnet" with CIDR "10.0.2.0/24" in a second availability zone. Provision an internet gateway named "development-be-ig" and a public route table named "development-be-public-rt" that sends internet-bound traffic through the gateway and is associated only with the public subnet. Also create a security group named "http_access" (tagged "development-be-sg") that allows SSH only from within the VPC CIDR, allows HTTP on port 80 from anywhere, and restricts all outbound traffic to the VPC CIDR, and output the VPC and both subnet IDs.

We need a Terraform template that creates a feature-rich, production-grade Amazon SNS topic module with customizable access policies, subscriptions, protocol feedback logging, and data protection rules to handle asynchronous application messaging. Entire stack deployment must be toggled via a create boolean variable defaulting to true. The core topic component must accept a name string variable (defaulting to null) and a use_name_prefix boolean (defaulting to false) to set either name or name_prefix, alongside settings for content-based deduplication (defaulting to false), delivery policy, display name, KMS encryption key ID, signature version (set to null if fifo_topic is true), tracing configuration, and FIFO enablement (defaulting to false). We need a Terraform template that creates a feature-complete Amazon S3 bucket module supporting dynamic naming, encryption, website hosting, access control, lifecycle management, CORS, logging, replication, and object lock configurations. The bucket name must derive from an optional bucket_name variable, falling back to "corebucket-" appended with a 4-byte random hexadecimal string if null, and appending an extra random string suffix when a boolean prefix variable is true. Key parameters must default as follows: request_payer to "BucketOwner", encryption to true, kms_key to an empty string (in which case the module creates its own rotating customer-managed KMS key, so encryption is always "aws:kms" with either the supplied key ARN or the module-created key), versioning, mfa_delete, force_destroy, and prefix to false, always blocking all public access on the bucket, while allowing optional overrides for ACLs, JSON policy documents, grants, tags, transfer acceleration status, logging target bucket and prefix, website index/error documents or redirect-all rules, CORS rules, lifecycle rules, and object lock configurations (supporting compliance/governance default retention modes and periods). Additionally, when replication_rules are supplied, the module must configure cross-region replication rules; if no external replication_role ARN is provided, it must automatically create a dedicated IAM role named "CoreS3ReplicationRole_" followed by the resolved bucket name assumed by "s3.amazonaws.com" with a custom policy "CoreS3ReplicationPolicy_" followed by the resolved bucket name permitting bucket list/replication actions and attach it directly to the role.

We need a Terraform template that creates a self-contained Amazon S3 datastore storage stack with scoped IAM read-only access for application image hosting. The template must support optional random suffix generation using a lowercase alphanumeric string (length defaulting to 4, special characters disabled, controlled by a random_suffix boolean defaulting to true) to append to the S3 bucket name (defaulting to "zedcloud"), IAM username (defaulting to "zedcloud-s3-user"), and IAM policy name (defaulting to "zedcloud-s3-policy"). The S3 bucket must be created with force_destroy enabled, tagged with its resolved name, and encrypted by default with SSE-KMS using a customer-managed KMS key with rotation enabled, and restricted using an S3 public access block that enables all public access blocking parameters (block_public_acls, ignore_public_acls, block_public_policy, and restrict_public_buckets). An image upload resource must be conditionally created based on an upload_image boolean (defaulting to false), referencing a local image source file specified by image_filename (defaulting to "my-file.qcow2") located in the execution directory and uploading it to an S3 key path that prefixes the filename with s3_folder (defaulting to "my-folder") if create_folder (defaulting to true) is set. Additionally, IAM user creation must be toggled via create_iam_user (defaulting to true), provisioning an IAM user with force_destroy set to true under path "/", an active IAM access key, an IAM policy granting s3:GetObject on bucket objects and s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN, and an IAM user policy attachment linking the policy to the user.

We need a Terraform template that creates a multi-AZ Amazon EKS-ready VPC networking foundation to host Kubernetes cluster workloads. The configuration must apply provider-level default tags using a default_tags map variable containing keys for Project ("tf-eks-jofo"), Owner ("Jovan Zelincevic"), Compliance ("Nothing"), Environment ("dev"), and Provider ("Terraform"). Provision a main VPC with default instance tenancy, enabled DNS support, enabled DNS hostnames, and a CIDR block of "10.14.0.0/16", named according to the project and environment tags. Across the first three available availability zones in the region, create three public subnets with public IP mapping disabled using calculated /20 CIDR blocks starting at index 0, associated with a dedicated public route table configured with an internet gateway route for "0.0.0.0/0". Additionally, provision three private subnets across the same three availability zones using consecutive /20 CIDR blocks continuing after the public subnets, associated with a private route table routing "0.0.0.0/0" traffic through a single NAT gateway deployed in the first public subnet with an allocated Elastic IP.

We need a Terraform template that creates a highly configurable Amazon S3 bucket module supporting advanced access logging, static website hosting, cross-region replication, lifecycle management, object locking, and custom bucket policy controls. The stack must be governed by a boolean create_bucket variable defaulting to true and support bucket or bucket_prefix naming options, canned ACLs defaulting to "private", force_destroy options defaulting to false, tags, acceleration_status, request_payer, and object ownership controls defaulting to "ObjectWriter" when control_object_ownership is set. It must dynamically process website hosting, CORS rules, bucket versioning, access logging, policy grants, object lifecycle rules, cross-region replication, server-side encryption, and object locking. When no server-side encryption configuration is supplied, the module must create its own customer-managed KMS key with automatic rotation and a seven-day deletion window and apply it as the bucket's default SSE-KMS encryption. Additionally, the template must conditionally construct and attach a combined bucket policy combining ELB log delivery permissions (when attach_elb_log_delivery_policy is true), ALB/NLB log delivery write and ACL check permissions (when attach_lb_log_delivery_policy is true), non-SSL transport denial (when attach_deny_insecure_transport_policy is true), and a custom policy document string (when attach_policy is true). Finally, it must support an S3 public access block resource toggled via an attach_public_policy variable defaulting to true to control block_public_acls, block_public_policy, ignore_public_acls, and restrict_public_buckets parameters.

We need a Terraform template that creates a multi-subnet VPC network stack distributed across two availability zones for infrastructure testing. The template must define variables for tagging including projectPrefix (defaulting to "f5-dcec"), resourceOwner (defaulting to "f5-user"), buildSuffix (defaulting to "YY"), and map_public_ip_on_launch (defaulting to false), alongside an awsRegion variable defaulting to "us-east-1". Two optional availability zone variables (awsAz1 and awsAz2, both defaulting to null) must resolve to the first and second available availability zones in the region if unassigned, noting a logic requirement where awsAz2 falls back to referencing awsAz1 when specified. The core VPC must use a CIDR block configurable via vpcMainCidr (defaulting to "10.1.0.0/16"). Across the two resolved availability zones, create six total subnets: two public subnets using vpcMainSubPubACidr ("10.1.10.0/24") and vpcMainSubPubBCidr ("10.1.110.0/24") mapped with the map_public_ip_on_launch setting; two management subnets using vpcMainSubMgmtACidr ("10.1.1.0/24") and vpcMainSubMgmtBCidr ("10.1.101.0/24"); and two private subnets using vpcMainSubPrivACidr ("10.1.20.0/24") and vpcMainSubPrivBCidr ("10.1.120.0/24"). Additionally, create an internet gateway for the VPC, a custom route table routing all outbound traffic "0.0.0.0/0" to the internet gateway, and assign this route table explicitly as the VPC main route table association.

We need a Terraform template that creates an internal Application Load Balancer setup for testing path-based routing in a self-contained network. The infrastructure must be provisioned within a VPC having the CIDR block "10.0.0.0/16" and two subnets distributed across the first two available availability zones in the region using calculated /24 CIDR blocks. Deploy an internal Application Load Balancer that drops invalid header fields, using a security group that allows all ingress and egress traffic within the VPC CIDR, an HTTP target group on port 8080 configured with an HTTP health check on port 8081 at path "/health" (with an interval of 60 seconds, a timeout of 3 seconds, a matcher of "200-299", and healthy/unhealthy thresholds of 3), and an HTTPS listener on port 443 (TLS 1.3 security policy, self-signed certificate imported into ACM) forwarding to the target group. Additionally, create a configurable number of listener rules (governed by a resource count variable defaulting to 1) that forward traffic matching the path pattern "/static-N/*" (where N is the rule index, starting at 0) to the target group, starting at priority 100. All named resources must default to using the resource name "benchmark", and the region variable must default to "us-east-1".

We need a Terraform template that creates a secure, centralized audit logging infrastructure using AWS CloudTrail to record all management events across the environment for compliance monitoring. The solution must configure an AWS CloudTrail instance whose name is controlled by a variable defaulting to "management_trail", enabled as a multi-region trail with log file validation, global service event tracking, management event filtering covering all read/write types, and optional organization trail behavior toggled via a boolean variable defaulting to false. CloudTrail logs must deliver to a newly provisioned S3 bucket whose name appends a 12-digit numeric random string to "cloudtrail-bucket-", encrypted by default with SSE-KMS using the customer managed CloudTrail KMS key, blocked from all public access, and attached to a bucket policy permitting CloudTrail to perform GetBucketAcl and PutObject with bucket-owner-full-control checks. Additionally, streams must be forwarded to a dedicated CloudWatch Log Group named via a variable defaulting to "cloudtrail_logs" with retention set to never expire (0 days), integrated using an IAM role named "CloudTrailRoleForCloudWatchLogs" with an inline policy named "allow-access-to-cw-logs" permitting CloudTrail to create log streams and put log events. Finally, KMS encryption is governed by a boolean variable defaulting to true, which provisions a customer managed KMS key used for both the trail and the log bucket, with a key alias defaulting to "alias/cloudtrail_key" and a key policy allowing account root and caller identity administration, CloudTrail data key generation and key description, S3 use of the key for bucket encryption, and account-wide log decryption rights.

We need a Terraform template that creates a managed Amazon ECR container repository with associated IAM access policies and lifecycle management for application image storage. The repository name must combine an optional namespace variable (defaulting to empty) and repository name variable (defaulting to "ecr" using frigga naming conventions with petname generation when null or empty) separated by a forward slash, tagged with "terraform.io" set to "managed" and a "Name" tag matching the repository name path. The repository configuration must support customizable image tag mutability defaulting to "IMMUTABLE", image scan on push defaulting to true, and a lifecycle policy that is only created when a lifecycle_policy JSON string is supplied (defaulting to null, so no lifecycle policy is created by default). Additionally, the module must provision an IAM policy named "<local_name>-ecr-read" allowing ecr:BatchCheckLayerAvailability, ecr:BatchGetImage, ecr:DescribeImages, ecr:DescribeRepositories, ecr:GetAuthorizationToken, ecr:GetDownloadUrlForLayer, and ecr:ListImages on the repository ARN; an IAM policy named "<local_name>-ecr-write" allowing ecr:PutImage, ecr:UploadLayerPart, ecr:InitiateLayerUpload, and ecr:CompleteLayerUpload on the repository ARN; and an ECR repository policy titled "AllowCrossAccountAccess" granting read access to the current caller account and any additional AWS account IDs supplied in a trusted_accounts list variable.

We need a Terraform template that creates a highly dynamic VPC network infrastructure for multi-tier application deployments. The setup must feature a base VPC CIDR block defaulting to "10.0.0.0/16" and configurable toggles for enabling public, NAT, and private subnet tiers across a specified number of available availability zones in the region, which defaults to 2. Subnet CIDRs across all enabled tiers must be calculated dynamically using log-based bitwise splitting based on the total active subnet count across availability zones. If public subnets are enabled, the infrastructure must automatically provision auto-assigning public IP subnets, an Internet Gateway, a dedicated security group with an egress rule allowing all traffic across all protocols to 0.0.0.0/0, and a public route table containing an internet route to 0.0.0.0/0 via the Internet Gateway alongside a local VPC CIDR route attached to all public subnets. Furthermore, enabling NAT or private subnet options must independently provision their respective subnet sets across the configured availability zones using offset CIDR calculations.

We need a Terraform template that creates a custom VPC environment to host data processing workloads with public and private subnet structures and SSH bastion access capabilities. The network configuration must default to a primary VPC CIDR block of "10.0.0.0/16" with DNS support and DNS hostnames enabled, paired with an Internet Gateway named "demogwInternet", a public route table named "demoPublicRouteTable" sending all outbound traffic to 0.0.0.0/0 via the gateway, and a set of public subnets that do not auto-assign public IPs on launch, mapped across specified availability zones using default CIDRs "10.0.0.0/24" and "10.0.2.0/24". The template should also define standard configurable variables with proper default values for project ("demo"), environment ("poc"), VPC name ("demo-dataflow"), region ("us-east-1"), private subnet CIDR blocks ("10.0.1.0/24" and "10.0.3.0/24"), EC2 key pair name ("kplinuxdemo"), bastion instance type ("t3.nano"), EBS optimization toggle (false), and custom resource tagging maps.

We need a Terraform template that creates a comprehensive AWS Backup solution for all RDS databases in the account, with four backup schedules: daily (retained 7 days, triggered at 2 AM UTC), weekly (retained 30 days, triggered Saturdays at 2 AM UTC), monthly (retained 365 days, triggered on the 1st at 3 AM UTC), and yearly (retained 2555 days, triggered on January 1st at 4 AM UTC), each using KMS-encrypted backup vaults and including a copy action to a cross-region vault in a configurable secondary AWS region, plus an optional cross-account copy to a specified destination account (defaulting to account ID 433568766270) when enabled via a boolean variable that defaults to true; the solution must also create the necessary IAM role with the AWS Backup service role policy, allow excluding specific RDS instances by ARN via a list variable, and use a variable to control whether the daily backup plan is created (defaulting to true).

We need a Terraform template that creates a comprehensive AWS IAM user management and security baseline stack to govern role-based access control and password compliance across environments. The template must configure an account password policy with variables defaulting to allowing user password changes (true), non-hard expiry (false), maximum password age of 90 days, minimum password length of 14 characters, password reuse prevention history of 24, and required lowercase, uppercase, number, and symbol characters (all true). It must provision three IAM groups named "administrators", "developpers", and "prod_users", each paired with an attached custom IAM policy. The "developpers_policy" attached to "developpers" must allow full EC2 ("ec2:*") and RDS ("rds:*") actions on all resources conditioned on matching the resource tag "env" equal to "dev". The "prod_users_policy" attached to "prod_users" must allow full EC2 and RDS actions on all resources conditioned on matching the resource tag "env" equal to "preprod" or "prod". The "administrators_policy" attached to "administrators" must grant broad access on all resources using a NotAction block that excludes "iam:*", "organizations:*", and "account:*" conditioned on the resource tag "security" not equaling "high", while explicitly permitting "iam:CreateServiceLinkedRole", "iam:DeleteServiceLinkedRole", "iam:ListRoles", "organizations:DescribeOrganization", and "account:ListRegions" across all resources.

We need a Terraform template that creates an isolated private VPC networking infrastructure with S3 gateway endpoint access for secure internal workloads. The stack must deploy a VPC configured with a variable region defaulting to "us-east-1", a resource name prefix variable defaulting to "tfm-aws", instance tenancy defaulting to "default", enabled DNS hostnames (true), enabled DNS support (true), and a main CIDR block defaulting to "10.0.0.0/16". Provision two private subnets across the first two available availability zones in the region using CIDR blocks specified by a private_subnets list variable defaulting to ["10.0.2.0/24", "10.0.3.0/24"], paired with two dedicated private route tables and subnet route table associations. Additionally, associate an S3 VPC gateway endpoint with both private route tables, and associate a shared network ACL with the private subnets containing an inbound rule and an outbound rule configured from variable lists public_inbound_acl_rules and public_outbound_acl_rules (the inbound rule defaulting to rule number 100 allowing TCP ports 1024 to 65535 from "0.0.0.0/0" for return traffic, and the outbound rule defaulting to rule number 100 allowing only TCP port 443 to "0.0.0.0/0").

We need a Terraform template that creates a customizable, self-contained AWS VPC base networking module supporting dual-stack IPv4/IPv6 IPAM allocations, default adoption rule resets, and internet gateways using Cloud Posse null-label context conventions. The core VPC resource must accept a primary IPv4 CIDR block defaulting to "11.0.0.0/16" (or an optional IPAM pool association), instance tenancy defaulting to "default", enabled DNS hostnames (true), enabled DNS support (true), and autogenerated IPv6 CIDR block assignment defaulting to true (with support for optional primary IPv6 IPAM associations). The stack must allow registering additional IPv4 and IPv6 CIDR block associations from map variables (supporting IPAM pools, netmask lengths, and creation/deletion timeouts). To enforce security baselines, default resource management features must allow adoption of default VPC resources, including a default security group that strips all rules when a default_security_group_deny_all variable is set to true, alongside configurable adoption flags for default route tables (defaulting to false) and default network ACLs (defaulting to false). Finally, the template must conditionally provision a standard IPv4/IPv6 internet gateway controlled by an internet_gateway_enabled boolean defaulting to true and an IPv6 egress-only internet gateway controlled by an ipv6_egress_only_internet_gateway_enabled boolean defaulting to false.

We need a Terraform template that creates a self-contained IAM security framework for provisioning infrastructure deployment credentials and scoped EC2/backend permissions. The stack must deploy an IAM user with force_destroy enabled using a username variable defaulting to "my_vpn_infra_user", an IAM group defined by group_name defaulting to "my-vpn-infra-group", group membership defined by membership_name defaulting to "my-vpn-infra-manager-group", and an active IAM access key for the user. All created policies and the IAM user must apply a ProjectTag tag matching a project_tag variable defaulting to "my-vpn-tag", and all policies must be attached to the IAM group using a custom policy path variable defaulting to "/my_vpn_infra/". The template must create seven distinct IAM policies attached to the group: basic_policy granting "sts:GetCallerIdentity"; create_policy granting explicit EC2 resource creation actions ("ec2:CreateKeyPair", "ec2:CreateVpc", "ec2:CreateSubnet", "ec2:CreateInternetGateway", "ec2:CreateRoute", "ec2:CreateRouteTable", "ec2:CreateLocalGatewayRouteTableVpcAssociation", "ec2:CreateSecurityGroup", "ec2:AuthorizeSecurityGroupEgress", "ec2:AuthorizeSecurityGroupIngress", "ec2:CreateReplaceRootVolumeTask", "ec2:CreateTags", and "ec2:AllocateAddress"); read_policy granting a comprehensive set of EC2 read actions; update_policy granting EC2 modification and association actions; delete_policy granting EC2 deletion and detachment actions; instance_policy granting EC2 lifecycle actions ("ec2:RunInstances", "ec2:StartInstances", "ec2:ResetInstanceAttribute", "ec2:ModifyInstanceAttribute", "ec2:StopInstances", "ec2:TerminateInstances", and "ec2:RebootInstances"); and terraform_backend_access granting DynamoDB state lock access ("dynamodb:DescribeTable", "dynamodb:GetItem", "dynamodb:PutItem", and "dynamodb:DeleteItem") alongside S3 backend access ("s3:ListBucket", "s3:GetObject", "s3:PutObject", and "s3:DeleteObject") on all resources.

We need a Terraform template that creates a dual-tier VPC networking stack in region "us-east-1" to host public and private web workloads. The template must accept an optional existing_vpc_id variable defaulting to an empty string, falling back to creating a new VPC with enabled DNS hostnames, an environment prefix defaulting to "DEV", and a main CIDR block defaulting to "10.0.0.0/16". Provision two public subnets across two different availability zones in the region with CIDRs "10.0.1.0/24" and "10.0.2.0/24", associated with an internet gateway via a public route table routing "0.0.0.0/0". Additionally, include a boolean flag craete_private_subnet defaulting to false; when enabled, it must create two private subnets across the same two availability zones using CIDRs "10.0.10.0/24" and "10.0.11.0/24", a private route table, and a single Elastic IP-backed NAT Gateway in the first public subnet (with Elastic IP private IP association defaulting to "10.0.0.5") routing outbound "0.0.0.0/0" traffic for the private subnets.

We need a Terraform template that creates a comprehensive Amazon SQS messaging module supporting standard and FIFO queues, custom queue policies, dead-letter queues, redrive policies, and SSE encryption. Primary queue creation must be controlled by a boolean variable create defaulting to true, handling name or name_prefix patterns while automatically managing the .fifo suffix for FIFO queues (fifo_queue defaulting to false). SQS managed server-side encryption (sqs_managed_sse_enabled defaulting to true) must apply automatically whenever a custom KMS master key ID is omitted. Option for attached queue policies must be governed by a create_queue_policy flag defaulting to false, merging source and override policy document strings or rendering custom policy statements where resource defaults to the queue ARN when unspecified. When dead-letter queue creation is toggled on via create_dlq (defaulting to false), the template must provision a corresponding dead-letter queue (inheriting FIFO configuration, default name suffixing "-dlq", and fallback encryption settings from the main queue), attach a redrive policy to the main queue setting maxReceiveCount to 5, and attach a redrive allow policy to the dead-letter queue restricting redrive permissions byQueue to the main queue ARN when create_dlq_redrive_allow_policy is true (defaulting to true).

We need a Terraform template that creates a self-contained IAM infrastructure for load balancer monitoring automation in the us-east-1 region. The stack must provision three system IAM users named "loadbalancer", "loadbalancer2", and "loadbalancer3", all created under the path "/system/" and equipped with active programmatic access keys. Each user must have four individual inline user policies attached directly to them granting "ec2:Describe*" permissions across all resources; specifically, user "loadbalancer" must have inline policies named "test", "test2", "test3", and "test4", user "loadbalancer2" must have inline policies named "test2", "test22", "test23", and "test24", and user "loadbalancer3" must have inline policies named "test3", "test32", "test33", and "test34".

We need a Terraform template that creates an AWS Backup vault infrastructure supporting multi-account patterns with customizable retention locking, SNS notifications, and workload-specific backup plans. The configuration must accept a required backup name variable, an account_type variable defaulting to "workload" (validated strictly to "workload" or "backup"), an optional KMS key ARN for vault encryption, and an optional vault policy string. When a min_retention_days parameter is provided, the template must configure a vault lock with optional max_retention_days and changeable_for_days. Optional vault notifications must be controlled by a boolean flag enable_aws_backup_vault_notifications (defaulting to false) to route failure events (defaulting to "BACKUP_JOB_FAILED" and "COPY_JOB_FAILED") to a specified SNS topic ARN. When account_type is set to "workload", the template must provision an IAM role prefixed with "aws-backup-" with the AWSBackupServiceRolePolicyForBackup managed policy attached, a backup plan named by combining "plan-" with the backup name value and the suffix "-backup", with configurable rule schedule, 60-minute start window, 120-minute completion window, cold storage transition after 30 days, deletion after 120 days, recovery point tagging, and dynamic cross-region or cross-account copy actions, alongside a tag-based backup selection matching key "Backup" equal to "true" using "STRINGEQUALS" and an additional resource-based selection if explicit ARNs are supplied in selection_resources.

We need a Terraform template that creates an AWS Config compliance auditing and security monitoring stack to track configuration changes and enforce security rules across all supported resources in the account. The stack must deploy an IAM role using a name generated from a naming convention module (defaulting to "config" with petname fallback when null or empty) paired with the AWS_ConfigRole managed policy, write permissions to a force-destroy-enabled S3 snapshot storage bucket, and an inline policy permitting SNS publish operations. An AWS Config configuration recorder must capture all supported global and regional resource types and deliver snapshot records with an S3 key prefix of "awsconfig/records" to the snapshot bucket while streaming notifications to an SNS topic bearing the resource name that is encrypted with a dedicated customer-managed KMS key with automatic rotation. Additionally, the template must provision a set of eleven managed AWS Config rules evaluated every twenty-four hours or upon configuration changes: "cloudtrail-enabled" (CLOUD_TRAIL_ENABLED), "iam-pw-policy" (IAM_PASSWORD_POLICY), "ec2-vpc" (INSTANCES_IN_VPC), "root-mfa-enabled" (ROOT_ACCOUNT_MFA_ENABLED), "acm-expiration-check" (ACM_CERTIFICATE_EXPIRATION_CHECK), "ebs-inuse-check" (EC2_VOLUME_INUSE_CHECK), "ec2-imdsv2-check" (EC2_IMDSV2_CHECK), "rds-encrypted" (RDS_STORAGE_ENCRYPTED), "rds-private" (RDS_INSTANCE_PUBLIC_ACCESS_CHECK), "rds-private-snapshots" (RDS_SNAPSHOTS_PUBLIC_PROHIBITED), and "required-tags" (REQUIRED_TAGS checking for "terraform.io" and "environment" tags specifically scoped to "S3::Bucket" resources).

We need a Terraform template that creates a multi-tier VPC network across three availability zones to host web application, database, and caching workloads. The stack must deploy a VPC with CIDR block "10.0.0.0/16" with DNS hostnames and DNS support enabled, tagged with Name, Project ("BJIT DevOps Task"), and Author ("Ariful Islam"). Provision three public subnets with CIDR blocks "10.0.4.0/24", "10.0.6.0/24", and "10.0.8.0/24" that do not auto-assign public IP addresses, alongside three private subnets with CIDR blocks "10.0.10.0/24", "10.0.12.0/24", and "10.0.14.0/24", one of each per availability zone. Public subnets must share a public route table connected to an Internet Gateway, while each private subnet uses its own zone-specific private route table, and all private route tables are associated with an S3 gateway VPC endpoint. Additionally, create six security groups whose outbound traffic is limited to the VPC CIDR: "bjit-api-server-ALB-SG" allowing TCP ports 80 through 443 from anywhere; "bjit-mariaDB-RDS-SG" allowing MySQL/MariaDB (port 3306) from the VPC CIDR; "bjit-redis-SG" allowing Redis (port 6379) from the VPC CIDR; "bjit-api-server-SG" allowing ports 8080 and 22 from the VPC CIDR; "bjit-file-server-SG" allowing ports 8081 and 22 from the VPC CIDR; and "bjit-public-ssh-SG" allowing SSH (port 22) from the VPC CIDR.

We need a Terraform template that creates a scalable VPC network infrastructure with optional private subnet tiers, NAT gateways, and private VPC endpoints for secure container workloads. The template must construct a main VPC with enabled DNS hostnames using a base_name prefix variable defaulting to "benchmark" and a vpc_cidr block defaulting to "10.0.0.0/16". Public subnets must be provisioned using a subnet_public_cidrs list variable defaulting to ["10.0.1.0/24", "10.0.2.0/24"] across available availability zones starting from the second zone index, mapped to a public route table connected to an Internet Gateway with a default route for "0.0.0.0/0". Private subnets must be conditionally created based on a subnet_private_cidrs list variable defaulting to null; when private CIDRs are provided, the template must provision private subnets across matching availability zone indices, create per-public-subnet Elastic IPs and NAT Gateways with corresponding private route table entries for "0.0.0.0/0", and associate a dedicated private gateway endpoint for S3. Furthermore, the infrastructure must include an S3 gateway endpoint for public subnets, as well as HTTPS interface VPC endpoints for ECR API and ECR Docker with private DNS enabled, bound to an ECR security group that allows egress only within the VPC CIDR and permits ingress on port 443 from all public subnet CIDRs and conditionally permits ingress on port 443 from private subnet CIDRs when private subnets are present.

We need a Terraform template that creates a self-contained, multi-tier AWS VPC network infrastructure across two availability zones to host secure web application and database tiers. The VPC must use a default CIDR block of "10.0.0.0/16" named "project-vpc", containing two public subnets ("pub-sub-1" with default CIDR "10.0.1.0/24" and "pub-sub-2" with default CIDR "10.0.2.0/24") and two private subnets ("pvt-sub-1" with default CIDR "10.0.3.0/24" and "pvt-sub-2" with default CIDR "10.0.4.0/24") deployed across the first two available availability zones in the region. An Internet Gateway named "T-igw" must connect two dedicated public route tables ("RT_PUBRT-1" and "RT_PUBRT-2") routing default outbound traffic ("0.0.0.0/0") for each public subnet. Provision two Elastic IPs and two NAT Gateways (both tagged "T-NAT1") in the respective public subnets; both private subnets must associate with dedicated private route tables ("RT_PVTRT-1" and "RT_PVTRT-2") that route default outbound traffic ("0.0.0.0/0") through the first NAT Gateway. Additionally, configure a public security group named "allow_tls" permitting inbound HTTP (port 80) and HTTPS (port 443) from everywhere ("0.0.0.0/0") and SSH (port 22) only from the placeholder admin range "203.0.113.0/24", with egress limited to the VPC CIDR, paired with a private security group named "pvt-seg" permitting inbound HTTP, HTTPS, SSH, and PostgreSQL (port 5432) traffic exclusively from the public security group and restricting egress exclusively to the public security group.

We need a Terraform template that creates a serverless, direct API Gateway to DynamoDB integration pattern to manage a pet inventory database without relying on Lambda functions. The stack must deploy a provisioned DynamoDB table named "Pets" with a primary hash key "id" (string) set to 5 read and 5 write capacity units, alongside a global secondary index named "PetType-index" on hash key "PetType" (string) projecting non-key attributes "PetName" and "PetPrice" with 5 read and 5 write capacity units. An IAM role assuming the "apigateway.amazonaws.com" service principal must grant permissions for "dynamodb:PutItem" and "dynamodb:Query" targeting the table and its indexes. Configure an API Gateway REST API named "APIGW DynamoDB Serverless Pattern Demo" enforcing API key security via an "x-api-key" header; it must expose a POST endpoint at "/pets" integrating directly with DynamoDB PutItem using VTL request templates mapping request payloads into "Pets" items with auto-generated requestId values and PetBoolean set to true, as well as a GET endpoint at "/pets/{PetType}" integrating directly with DynamoDB Query against "PetType-index" with URL-decoded parameter substitution and VTL response mapping. The REST API must be deployed to a stage named "v1" with method settings enabling INFO level CloudWatch logging and metrics, linked to an API Gateway account CloudWatch role, a CloudWatch log group prefixed with "/aws/APIGW/terraform", and a log resource policy permitting log delivery from the REST API source ARN. Finally, security must be enforced by provisioning an API key named "apigw-dynamodb-terraform-api-key" bound to a usage plan named "apigw-dynamodb-terraform-usage-plan" configured with a burst limit of 20, rate limit of 100, and a monthly quota limit of 1000 requests associated with stage "v1".

We need a Terraform template that creates a customizable Amazon S3 storage architecture for testing security configurations and public access policies using a configurable name variable defaulting to "sadcloud". The primary bucket must be constructed with force_destroy enabled, a prefix derived from the name variable, object ownership set to "BucketOwnerPreferred", a private ACL, and versioning enabled by default unless a boolean variable no_versioning (defaulting to false) is set to true. The main bucket must have all public access blocked, and server-side encryption using a dedicated customer-managed KMS key with automatic rotation must be applied to it unless a boolean variable no_default_encryption (defaulting to false) disables it, and static website hosting with index document "index.html" must be conditionally configured based on a website_enabled boolean variable (defaulting to false). Logging for the main bucket must target a separate, force-destroy-enabled logging bucket named using the name value followed by the suffix "-logging", object ownership "BucketOwnerPreferred", and canned ACL defaulting to "log-delivery-write" (as defined by a bucket_acl variable), all public access blocked, and its own rotating customer-managed KMS key for default encryption, both of which are omitted if a no_logging boolean variable (defaulting to false) is set to true. Additionally, when an allow_cleartext boolean variable (defaulting to false) is true, attach an S3 bucket policy to the main bucket that explicitly denies all s3:* actions over non-SSL transport ("aws:SecureTransport" equal to "false"). Finally, the template must support optional secondary buckets with public access block restrictions completely disabled: one for public read-only access (s3_getobject_only defaulting to false) named using the name value followed by the suffix "-getonly" and an s3:GetObject policy, and another for full public read-write access (s3_public defaulting to false) named using the name value followed by the suffix "-public" and an s3:* policy.

We need a Terraform template that creates a self-contained IAM role and policy baseline required to initialize and operate AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery (DRS) across replication, conversion, failback, and recovery instances. The stack must provision six service roles under the "/service-role/" path: AWSElasticDisasterRecoveryAgentRole and AWSElasticDisasterRecoveryFailbackRole (both allowing drs.amazonaws.com to assume the role and set source identity, conditioned on the calling account ID and source identity prefixes "s-" and "i-", respectively), alongside AWSElasticDisasterRecoveryConversionServerRole, AWSElasticDisasterRecoveryRecoveryInstanceRole, AWSElasticDisasterRecoveryReplicationServerRole, and AWSElasticDisasterRecoveryRecoveryInstanceWithLaunchActionsRole (all assuming ec2.amazonaws.com). Attach corresponding AWS-managed policies (AWSElasticDisasterRecoveryAgentPolicy, AWSElasticDisasterRecoveryFailbackPolicy, AWSElasticDisasterRecoveryConversionServerPolicy, AWSElasticDisasterRecoveryRecoveryInstancePolicy, and AWSElasticDisasterRecoveryReplicationServerPolicy) to their respective service roles, while attaching both AWSElasticDisasterRecoveryRecoveryInstancePolicy and AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore to AWSElasticDisasterRecoveryRecoveryInstanceWithLaunchActionsRole. Finally, create a root-path initializer role named AWSElasticDisasterRecoveryInitializerRole that allows the current calling identity user ID to assume it, bound to a custom InitializePolicy permitting service initialization, instance profile creation, PassRole actions for EC2 and DRS services, service-linked role creation for AWSServiceRoleForElasticDisasterRecovery, full EC2 actions, and role policy attachments restricted to the DRS managed policies.

We need a Terraform template that creates a self-contained AWS VPC infrastructure for launching private compute instances in region "us-east-1". The network configuration must provision a VPC with a default CIDR block of "10.0.0.0/16" named "VPC_from_Terraform" with DNS support and DNS hostnames enabled, tagged "Terraform" set to "true". Three private subnets must be created using CIDR blocks ["10.0.1.0/24", "10.0.2.0/24", "10.0.3.0/24"] mapped across three availability zones. A security group named "allow_ssh_http_https" tagged "Terraform_SG_HTTP_HTTPS_SSH" must be attached to the VPC, allowing inbound SSH (port 22) restricted strictly to the VPC's CIDR block, inbound HTTP (port 80) and HTTPS (port 443) from everywhere ("0.0.0.0/0"), and egress limited to the VPC's CIDR block. Finally, deploy a default count of 3 EC2 instances of type "t2.micro" using the latest Amazon Linux 2 AMI by default, distributed across the private subnets with the security group attached, named "Terraform_Instance", and configured with an encrypted 20 GB root volume tagged "Terraform_EBS_Volume1" and IMDSv2 required.

We need a Terraform template that creates a comprehensive set of IAM roles and custom policies to support containerized application deployments on Amazon ECS with automated scaling and CodeDeploy blue/green deployments. The module must provision five specific IAM roles: "ecsServiceRole" allowing ecs.amazonaws.com and s3.amazonaws.com to assume it, attached to an inline policy "ecsTaskRolePolicy" granting permissions for ELB, EC2, SSM, Secrets Manager, KMS, CodeDeploy, SNS, CloudWatch, and Lambda operations; "ecsExecTaskRole" allowing ecs-tasks.amazonaws.com and s3.amazonaws.com to assume it, attached to inline policies "ecsExecRolePolicy" granting ECR, ECS service description, CloudWatch logging, Secrets Manager, KMS, and SSM permissions, alongside "ecsExecution_additional" granting ECS service listing and description plus S3 object read/write access; "ecsTaskRole" allowing ecs-tasks.amazonaws.com and s3.amazonaws.com to assume it, attached to an inline policy "ecsTaskRole_additional" granting ECS service listing and description plus S3 object read/write access; "ecs_autoscale_role" allowing application-autoscaling.amazonaws.com to assume it, attached to an inline policy "ecs_autoscale_role_policy" granting ECS service description and update access alongside CloudWatch alarm permissions; and "ecs_codedeploy_role" allowing codedeploy.amazonaws.com to assume it, attached to the AWSCodeDeployRole managed policy as well as inline policies "ecs_codedeploy_role_policy" for ECS task set, ELB, Lambda, CloudWatch, SNS, and S3 access, and separate PassRole policies ("ecs_codedeploy_role_policy_task" and "ecs_codedeploy_role_policy_task_exec") targeting the task and execution role ARNs.

We need a Terraform template that creates a dual-VPC isolated production network architecture consisting of an external VPC and an internal VPC in the region to segregate public-facing traffic from internal workloads. The external VPC must be configured with CIDR block "10.41.0.0/16", enable DNS support and DNS hostnames, apply tags for Name ("Production External"), purpose ("Production External VPC"), and environment ("prod"), and manage its default security group with no ingress or egress rules. Four subnets must be provisioned in the external VPC across the first four availability zones in the region using CIDR blocks "10.41.0.0/24" ("Subnet0-1a"), "10.41.1.0/24" ("Subnet1-1b"), "10.41.2.0/24" ("Subnet2-1c"), and "10.41.3.0/24" ("Subnet3-1d"), all attached to an Internet Gateway named "External GW" via a custom route table that is set as the main route table association for the VPC and associated with all four subnets. The external VPC default network ACL must adopt rules for ICMP egress (rule 100 allow), all-traffic egress (rule 150 allow), and all-traffic ingress (rule 100 allow) from "0.0.0.0/0". The internal VPC must be created with CIDR block "10.40.0.0/16", default tenancy, tags for Name ("Production Internal"), purpose ("Production Internal VPC"), and environment ("prod"), managing its default security group with no ingress or egress rules. Four internal subnets must be created in the internal VPC across the first four availability zones in the region using CIDR blocks "10.40.0.0/24" ("Subnet0-1a"), "10.40.1.0/24" ("Subnet1-1b"), "10.40.2.0/24" ("Subnet2-1c"), and "10.40.3.0/24" ("Subnet3-1d"), bound to a default network ACL that explicitly restricts rules to ICMP egress (rule 100 allow), all-traffic egress (rule 150 allow), and ICMP ingress (rule 100 allow) from "0.0.0.0/0".

We need a Terraform template that creates a self-contained, serverless deployment of n8n automation on AWS ECS Fargate with persistent EFS storage and an internal Application Load Balancer. The stack must build a VPC using CIDR "10.0.0.0/16" across the first three availability zones with three private subnets ("10.0.0.0/24", "10.0.1.0/24", "10.0.2.0/24") and three public subnets ("10.0.4.0/24", "10.0.5.0/24", "10.0.6.0/24"), with no NAT or VPN gateways. Configurable variables must include a resource prefix defaulting to "n8n", an optional certificate_arn defaulting to null, an optional url override defaulting to null, a desired_count defaulting to 1, a container_image defaulting to "n8nio/n8n:1.4.0", and a fargate_type defaulting to "FARGATE_SPOT". The internal Application Load Balancer must be placed in the public subnets, drop invalid header fields, and use a security group allowing inbound HTTP (port 80) and HTTPS (port 443) from anywhere, forwarding traffic to an IP target group on port 80 with a 30-second deregistration delay and a health check path of "/healthz" (2 healthy/unhealthy threshold, 3-second timeout, 30-second interval). An HTTPS listener on port 443 using "ELBSecurityPolicy-TLS13-1-2-2021-06" must always be created, using certificate_arn when provided and otherwise a self-signed certificate generated in the stack and imported into ACM, while the HTTP listener on port 80 redirects to HTTPS. An encrypted EFS file system must be provisioned with an access point rooted at "/n8n" (owner UID/GID 1000, 777 permissions) and mount targets in the private subnets, restricted to NFS port 2049 from the VPC CIDR. An ECS cluster with container insights disabled must use the chosen Fargate capacity provider with base 1 and weight 100 and run a service that places tasks in the public subnets with public IP assignment enabled and a security group allowing port 5678 only from the load balancer. The Fargate task definition must use 256 CPU and 512 memory, mount the EFS volume with transit encryption and IAM authorization to "/home/node/.n8n", and run an essential container on port 5678 that logs through the awslogs driver to a CloudWatch log group named with the prefix followed by "-logs" with 1-day retention, setting N8N_SKIP_WEBHOOK_DEREGISTRATION_SHUTDOWN to "true" and WEBHOOK_URL to the url variable or otherwise the HTTPS load balancer endpoint. All security groups must limit outbound traffic to the VPC CIDR. Finally, create task and execution IAM roles assumable by "ecs-tasks.amazonaws.com", each with an inline policy permitting CloudWatch log group and stream operations.

We need a Terraform template that creates an isolated AWS development network topology with dedicated subnets for database, application, and bastion host tiers. The stack must deploy a VPC named "lambda-rds-dev" with CIDR block "10.32.0.0/20" and DNS hostnames enabled, managing its default security group so that it has no ingress or egress rules, and setting up a default network ACL named "lambda-rds-dev-default-nacl" allowing all ingress and egress traffic. The subnets must be allocated across two availability zones: "lambda-rds-db-subnet-1" with CIDR "10.32.0.0/28" and "lambda-rds-dev-lambda-subnet" with CIDR "10.32.1.0/24" placed in the primary availability zone, "lambda-rds-db-subnet-2" with CIDR "10.32.0.16/28" placed in the secondary availability zone, and "lambda-rds-bastion-host-subnet" with CIDR "10.32.15.0/24" in the primary zone, without auto-assigning public IPs. An Internet Gateway named "lambda-rds-dev-igw" must connect to a public route table named "lambda-rds-public-subnet" routing "0.0.0.0/0" for the bastion subnet. Additionally, configure three security groups: "lambda-rds-dev-postgres-db" allowing egress strictly to "10.32.0.0/20" and ingress on PostgreSQL port 5432 from both the bastion and lambda security groups; "lambda-rds-dev-lambda-functions" allowing egress strictly to "10.32.0.0/20"; and "lambda-rds-dev-bastion-host" allowing inbound SSH on port 22 only from within the VPC CIDR block and egress restricted exclusively to the PostgreSQL database security group.

We need a Terraform template that creates a self-contained VPC networking baseline and security group configuration for a data stack environment supporting multi-AZ databases, bastion access, CI/CD automation, proxy load balancing, and ETL compute nodes. The VPC must be created with CIDR block "10.255.0.0/16" named "Quasar" and tagged with Application "dosomething-quasar", Environment "production", and Stack "data", housing two subnets for a multi-AZ RDS setup with CIDR blocks "10.255.100.0/24" (tagged Name "Quasar RDS - 1A") and "10.255.101.0/24" (tagged Name "Quasar RDS - 1E"). Five dedicated security groups with outbound egress limited to the VPC CIDR must be provisioned within the VPC using the same tagging schema: a "Quasar-Bastion" security group allowing inbound SSH (port 22) only from the placeholder admin range "203.0.113.0/24"; a "Quasar-HA-Proxy" security group allowing inbound HTTP (port 80) and HTTPS (port 443) from everywhere ("0.0.0.0/0") and SSH (port 22) from the Bastion security group; a "Quasar-Jenkins" security group allowing inbound SSH (port 22) from the Bastion security group and port 8080 from the HA-Proxy security group; a "Quasar-ETL" security group allowing inbound SSH (port 22) from both the Bastion and Jenkins security groups; and a "Quasar-PostgreSQL" security group allowing inbound PostgreSQL traffic (port 5432) both from everywhere ("0.0.0.0/0") and specifically referenced from the ETL security group.

We need a Terraform template that creates a versatile Amazon SQS messaging infrastructure module supporting configurable standard or FIFO queues, managed encryption, redrive policies, and optional dead-letter queue (DLQ) provisioning. Overall module creation must be governed by a boolean create variable defaulting to true, accepting a human-readable queue name variable stripped of any ".fifo" suffix, with an option to use the name as a prefix via a boolean use_name_prefix variable defaulting to false. The primary queue must support FIFO settings including fifo_queue (defaulting to false), content_based_deduplication, deduplication_scope, and fifo_throughput_limit, alongside standard queue parameters for delay_seconds, max_message_size, message_retention_seconds, receive_wait_time_seconds, and visibility_timeout_seconds. Encryption for the primary queue must default to SQS-managed server-side encryption (sqs_managed_sse_enabled defaulting to true) unless a custom kms_master_key_id is provided alongside an optional kms_data_key_reuse_period_seconds. Queue policies for both the main queue and the DLQ must be conditionally created based on create_queue_policy and create_dlq_queue_policy boolean variables (both defaulting to false), allowing merged or overridden IAM policy documents and custom statement blocks. When create_dlq is set to true (defaulting to false), the template must provision an aligned dead-letter queue automatically inheriting the main queue's FIFO type, throughput limits, and base encryption settings unless overridden by specific DLQ parameters, using a default DLQ name suffix of "-dlq", automatically attaching a redrive policy to the main queue setting maxReceiveCount to 5 targeting the DLQ, and conditionally attaching a redrive allow policy to the DLQ restricting redrive permissions to "byQueue" for the source queue ARN when create_dlq_redrive_allow_policy is true (defaulting to true).

We need a Terraform template that creates an automated AWS CodeDeploy release pipeline for AWS Lambda blue/green deployments managed via local CLI execution scripts. Global creation controls must be governed by a boolean create variable defaulting to true, accepting a function_name, alias_name, current_version, and target_version alongside optional before_allow_traffic_hook_arn and after_allow_traffic_hook_arn lifecycle hooks. When create_app is true and use_existing_app is false (both defaulting to false), create a Lambda compute platform CodeDeploy application named by app_name, and when create_deployment_group is true and use_existing_deployment_group is false (both defaulting to false), provision a deployment group bound to deployment_config_name (defaulting to "CodeDeployDefault.LambdaAllAtOnce") configured with "WITH_TRAFFIC_CONTROL" and "BLUE_GREEN" deployment styles, automatic rollbacks enabled by default on "DEPLOYMENT_STOP_ON_ALARM", optional CloudWatch alarm monitoring, and notification triggers. When create_codedeploy_role is true (defaulting to true), the module must create an IAM role with assume policy for specified CodeDeploy service principals (defaulting to "codedeploy.amazonaws.com"), attach the "AWSCodeDeployRoleForLambda" managed policy, and conditionally attach inline policies granting lambda:InvokeFunction for specified hooks when attach_hooks_policy is true (defaulting to true) or sns:Publish for triggers when attach_triggers_policy is true (defaulting to false). Finally, when create_deployment is true (defaulting to false), construct an AppSpec JSON revision and shell script that uses aws_cli_command (defaulting to "aws") to create and optionally monitor the deployment status with configurable sleep intervals (defaulting get_deployment_sleep_timer to 5 seconds), optionally saving the generated script locally when save_deploy_script is true (defaulting to false) or executing the deployment provisioner via a null resource when run_deployment is true (defaulting to false) with optional uuid-based force_deploy triggers.

We need a Terraform template that creates a customizable, multi-tier VPC environment supporting web, application, database, and reserved subnets with configurable CIDR block lists and counts, where the VPC CIDR defaults to 10.16.0.0/16 with DNS hostnames and DNS support enabled, and a random integer between 1 and 100 appended to the VPC name tag prefix which defaults to "tf-project". Subnets should automatically map to a set of randomly shuffled availability zones dynamically selected from the target region based on a configurable maximum subnet count, with web subnets mapping public IPs on launch and routing traffic through a conditionally created internet gateway via a dedicated public route table.
