Additionally, store the ARN, table name, and stream ARN as String SSM parameters under "/file-service/dynamodb/invitations/" for "near-files-invitations", "/file-service/dynamodb/files/" for "near-files", "/hashes-service/dynamodb/hashes/" for "near-hashes", "/file-service/dynamodb/storage/" for "near-storage", and under "/wallet-service/dynamodb/wallets/" for "near-wallets".

We need a Terraform template that creates a self-contained chaos engineering environment on AWS Fault Injection Simulator, targeting a small EC2 Auto Scaling Group running behind a minimal VPC with a single public subnet. The template must provision the VPC, subnet, internet gateway, and routing, an Auto Scaling Group of EC2 instances running the latest Amazon ECS-optimized AMI from a launch template that requires IMDSv2 and gives each instance a public IP (the subnet itself does not auto-assign one), with SSH access restricted to an admin CIDR block and an accepted SSH public key, and a set of FIS experiment templates that inject failures against these resources: an API-level internal-error fault against EC2's DescribeImages API, an EBS volume I/O pause, EC2 CPU stress, EC2 instance termination, and network connectivity disruption on the subnet, all targeting resources by tag and none configured to auto-stop. Include an S3 bucket for FIS experiment logs with all public access blocked, SSE-KMS encryption using a customer-managed key that AWS log delivery may use, and a bucket policy allowing AWS log delivery, the IAM role that FIS assumes to run these experiments with the necessary fault-injection permissions, and the EC2 instance role and profile needed for the instances themselves to run under ECS and SSM.

We need a Terraform template that creates a highly modular AWS VPC infrastructure module supporting IPAM integration, customizable public and private subnets, DHCP options, NAT gateways, flow logs, and default resource governance. The primary VPC creation must be controlled by a create_vpc boolean variable defaulting to true, accepting an IPv4 CIDR block defaulting to "10.0.0.0/16" (or utilizing an IPAM pool via ipv4_ipam_pool_id and ipv4_netmask_length), supporting secondary IPv4 CIDR block associations, and enabling DNS hostnames and DNS support by default. Public and private subnet tiers must be defined via flexible map structures accepting explicit CIDR blocks, availability zone assignments, and IPv6 parameters, alongside dedicated route table definitions that map public subnet traffic through a conditionally created Internet Gateway (create_igw defaulting to true) or private subnet traffic through mapped NAT Gateways deployed with Elastic IPs. The module must support optional egress-only internet gateways for IPv6, customizable network ACLs (with private subnets supporting dedicated ACLs with default allow-all inbound and outbound rules), conditionally created DHCP option sets and associations, and VPC flow logs configured across log destinations with custom formatting and aggregation intervals. Finally, the template must allow adopting and managing default VPC components, specifically the default security group (manage_default_security_group defaulting to false), default network ACL (manage_default_network_acl defaulting to false with default allow rules for IPv4/IPv6), and default route table (manage_default_route_table defaulting to false), to enforce security compliance across the network boundary.

We need a Terraform template that creates a versatile AWS Transfer Family SFTP server solution supporting public or VPC-hosted endpoints, automated user provisioning, and optional Route 53 DNS mapping. The server identifier must derive from an explicit name variable or fallback to a two-word hyphenated random pet name, defaulting logging to a dynamically provisioned IAM role attached to "AWSTransferLoggingAccess" unless an explicit logging role ARN is provided. If configured for API Gateway authentication, the module must provision an API Gateway authorization IAM role with CloudWatch logging permissions. The server endpoint type must support "PUBLIC", "VPC", or "VPC_ENDPOINT" modes, defaulting to "PUBLIC" with "S3" storage and "SFTP" protocols, while supporting optional FTPS ACM certificates, custom login banners, custom security policies (defaulting to "TransferSecurityPolicy-2023-05"), host keys, structured CloudWatch log destinations, and protocol details for AS2, passive IP, set-stat options, or TLS session resumption. When hosted inside a VPC without pre-existing network resources supplied in endpoint details, it must automatically create a dedicated security group opening port 22 to 0.0.0.0/0 along with an Elastic IP per specified subnet. Furthermore, if a Route 53 hosted zone is specified, create a CNAME record mapping a sub-domain (defaulting to "sftp") to the Transfer Server endpoint. Finally, for each user in a map of SFTP users, provision an IAM role and policy granting list and object access to their specified S3 home directory bucket path, an AWS Transfer user, and associate any matching SSH public keys provided in a secondary user key map.

We need a Terraform template that creates the control plane of an Amazon EKS cluster named "md-k8s" inside a dedicated VPC with CIDR block 192.168.0.0/16 and DNS hostnames enabled. The VPC should be split into /19 subnets across up to three availability zones, with public subnets 192.168.0.0/19, 192.168.32.0/19, and 192.168.64.0/19 and private subnets 192.168.96.0/19, 192.168.128.0/19, and 192.168.160.0/19, none of which auto-assign public IP addresses and all tagged for Kubernetes load balancer discovery. Add an internet gateway with a public route table, a single NAT gateway with an Elastic IP in the first public subnet serving a shared private route table, and a database subnet group named "md-k8s-private-subnet-group" over the private subnets. The cluster must use a dedicated service role with the AWS-managed EKS cluster and VPC resource controller policies plus small custom policies for describing EC2 networking and publishing CloudWatch metrics, expose its API endpoint privately only, and envelope-encrypt Kubernetes secrets with a new customer-managed KMS key that has rotation enabled. Also create a control plane security group and a shared node security group that allows traffic between nodes and from the cluster's own security group, with outbound traffic on both limited to the VPC CIDR. No worker node group or Fargate profile is deployed.

We need a Terraform template that creates a highly configurable S3 bucket for general-purpose use, leveraging a label module for consistent resource naming and tagging, and always blocking all public access to the bucket, enabling versioning and server-side encryption by default (KMS encryption using a dedicated customer-managed KMS key with automatic rotation created by the template unless a key ID is supplied, or AES256 when KMS is disabled), and supporting optional features such as lifecycle configuration rules for transitions to STANDARD_IA, GLACIER, and DEEP_ARCHIVE as well as expiration and noncurrent version handling, bucket logging to a separate target bucket, static website hosting with index and error documents and routing rules, CORS rules, object lock configuration with default retention, bucket policies via an IAM policy document, acceleration status, requester pays, and fine-grained ACL grants or canned ACLs; the template should be self-contained, conditionally enabling each feature based on input variables, and must output the bucket ID, ARN, domain name, and tags.

We need a Terraform template that creates a VPC for application deployments, including public and private subnets, an internet gateway, a NAT gateway, route tables, and network ACLs. The VPC should use a CIDR block of 10.0.0.0/18. The number of availability zones should be configurable, defaulting to all available AZs in the region. The template should allow toggling the creation of public subnets, private subnets, and the NAT gateway via boolean variables. The VPC name should be configurable with a default of "benchmark-vpc". The AWS region should default to us-east-1. All necessary dependencies should be created as part of the stack.

We need a Terraform template that creates a multi-tier, dual-stack IPv4/IPv6 AWS network architecture to host a secure three-tier application environment. The stack must deploy a VPC tagged "main-vpc" with a default IPv4 CIDR block of "10.16.0.0/16", Amazon-provided IPv6 CIDR assignment enabled (controlled by is_ipv6_enabled defaulting to true), default instance tenancy, and both DNS hostnames and DNS support enabled by default. To calculate subnet allocations, the template must use the "hashicorp/subnets/cidr" module (version 1.0.0) to dynamically calculate IPv4 subnets using 4 additional bits (/20 subnets) and IPv6 subnets using 8 additional bits (/64 subnets) across a list of subnet objects (sn_details) containing subnet names, target availability zones, and public/private indicators, defaulting to 12 subnets across three availability zones for web (public), app (private), database (private), and reserved (private) tiers. An Internet Gateway tagged with a name prefixed by "main-igw-vpc-" followed by the VPC's resource ID must be attached to the VPC, and a public route table tagged "public-rt-web" routing all IPv4 ("0.0.0.0/0") and IPv6 ("::/0") traffic to the Internet Gateway must be created and associated exclusively with all subnets marked as public. Finally, security groups must be provisioned for each tier: a "web_sg" permitting ingress port 443 (TLS) from "0.0.0.0/0" and port 22 (SSH) only from the VPC IPv4 CIDR block and egress port 443 to "app_sg"; an "app_sg" permitting ingress port 443 from "web_sg" and egress port 443 to "db_sg"; and a "db_sg" permitting ingress port 443 from "app_sg".

We need a Terraform template that creates an automated CloudWatch Synthetics canary monitoring infrastructure to execute continuous health checks within a VPC and trigger notifications upon failure. The template must provision an execution IAM role with a randomized two-word pet name prefix for Lambda execution, granting S3 object read/write and bucket listing permissions, CloudWatch metric writing, CloudWatch logging, and EC2 ENI network interface management. An S3 bucket defaulting to "benchmark-canary-bucket-tf5x" with force destroy enabled, configurable versioning (defaulting to false), public access blocks, default CORS rules, and KMS server-side encryption must store canary artifacts. KMS key management should utilize an enable toggle (defaulting to true) for a custom KMS key with alias "alias/benchmark-canary-key", a 10-day deletion window, key rotation enabled, and a policy granting key access to CloudWatch and account root. An SNS topic named "benchmark-canary-topic" encrypted with the KMS key must publish failure notifications to an email subscription defaulting to "nobody@example.com", supported by an SNS topic policy allowing CloudWatch alarms to publish. The module must iterate over a map of VPC canary configurations to deploy CloudWatch Synthetics canaries inside specified subnet and security group lists, accepting either inline zip files or S3 artifact sources, with a 120-second execution timeout and configurable schedule expressions. Finally, each canary must include a CloudWatch metric failure alarm triggering on 1 or more failures in a 60-second period that sends alerts to the SNS topic, alongside an optional success percent metric alarm controlled by a boolean flag (defaulting to false) that sends OK notifications to the SNS topic when success falls below 90 percent.

We need a Terraform template that creates a highly customizable VPC module supporting multi-tier subnet architecture and configurable NAT gateway routing. The template must feature a main creation toggle defaulting to true, a configurable VPC CIDR block defaulting to "10.0.0.0/16", and options to enable DNS hostnames and DNS support (both defaulting to true). Subnet tiers must support lists of CIDR blocks for public, private, and isolated intra subnets mapped across a provided list of availability zone names or IDs, automatically generating subnet Name tags using configurable tier suffixes ("public", "private", "intra") and availability zone identifiers unless explicit name lists are supplied. When public subnets are present, the module should support map public IP on launch toggles (defaulting to false) and conditionally provision an Internet Gateway based on a creation toggle (defaulting to true) attached to a dedicated public route table with a default 0.0.0.0/0 route. Additionally, when private subnets, public subnets, and NAT gateways are enabled via the NAT gateway toggle (defaulting to false), the module must create Elastic IPs and NAT Gateways up to the minimum count of public or private subnets, establishing individual private route tables with 0.0.0.0/0 NAT routes associated with each private subnet, while intra subnets maintain isolated route tables without external internet routes.

We need a Terraform template that creates a unified, dual-mode API Gateway module capable of provisioning either an HTTP API (v2) or a REST API (v1) with optional VPC links, custom domain mappings, API keys, and custom Lambda authorizers. The API type must be determined by a variable defaulting to "http", using a default API name of "benchmark-api", and deploying stages named using the environment name value followed by the suffix "-stage". For HTTP APIs, the template should support dynamic route mappings, auto-deployed stages, custom domain configurations with TLS 1.2 regional ACM certificates, optional Route 53 alias A records, and HTTP VPC links created across private subnets. For REST APIs, the module must support dynamic resource path mapping, route methods with path parameter overrides, optional IP source restriction resource policies, automatic redeployment triggers, usage plans with API keys saved as SecureString parameters in SSM Parameter Store, and custom Lambda authorizers featuring Node.js 16.x functions, invocation roles, and execution policies. Additionally, when a VPC link is enabled for REST APIs, the setup must automatically provision an internal Network Load Balancer across private subnets, a target group targeting an ALB ID at a configurable TCP port (defaulting to 443) with HTTPS health checks, a target group attachment, a TCP listener, and an API Gateway VPC link targeting the load balancer ARN.

We need a Terraform template that creates a comprehensive, secure AWS CloudTrail logging architecture for auditing and compliance across account activities. The setup must provision a dedicated CloudTrail trail, an S3 log storage bucket, a CloudWatch Log Group, an IAM role for CloudWatch Logs ingestion, a KMS key for encryption, and an optional SNS notification topic. The S3 bucket name must default to dynamic generation incorporating account ID, region, and a random 8-character lowercase suffix if unspecified, with all public access blocked and default SSE-KMS encryption using the dedicated CloudTrail KMS key, featuring configurable force destroy (defaulting to true), versioning configuration (defaulting to false), and an S3 bucket policy permitting CloudTrail ACL checks and put-object actions with full control. CloudTrail log file encryption must use a dedicated KMS key with a 30-day deletion window, automated annual key rotation, an alias prefix, and a key policy granting permissions to root IAM users, CloudTrail encryption contexts, CloudWatch Logs, S3 bucket encryption, and an optional role ARN provided for log decryption. The CloudWatch Log Group must default to retaining logs for 90 days, populated by a dedicated IAM role and policy allowing CloudTrail to create log streams and put log events. CloudTrail itself must enforce log file validation, include global service events (defaulting to true), multi-region trails (defaulting to true), logging toggles (defaulting to true), organization trail toggles (defaulting to false), event selectors with configurable read/write types (defaulting to "All"), management events (defaulting to true), dynamic data resource selectors, and dynamic insight selectors. Finally, the module should support conditionally creating an SNS topic for alerts (disabled by default) with a topic policy allowing CloudTrail publishing, otherwise using an optional SNS topic ARN input that defaults to empty.

We need a Terraform template that creates a secure static website hosting architecture on AWS using Amazon S3, CloudFront, ACM, and Route 53. The infrastructure must provision a private S3 bucket (all public access blocked, default SSE-KMS encryption with a customer-managed key whose policy lets CloudFront decrypt objects for this distribution) whose name defaults to a custom name variable, falling back to an optional domain name variable, or an automated fallback name prefixed with "webapp-template-" appended with an 8-byte hexadecimal random ID if both are blank, with optional bucket versioning defaulting to false. CloudFront access to the bucket must be enforced using Origin Access Control with an S3 bucket policy allowing s3:GetObject strictly when the source ARN matches the CloudFront distribution ARN. The CloudFront distribution must be protected by a CloudFront-scoped WAFv2 web ACL (default action allow, metrics enabled) and must default to PriceClass_100, IPv6 enabled, index.html as the default root object, HTTPS redirection across all behaviors, and an origin signing protocol of SigV4. It must utilize the AWS-managed Managed-CachingOptimized cache policy by default while applying an ordered cache behavior with Managed-CachingDisabled specifically for the /index.html path, alongside default custom error responses mapping HTTP 403 and 404 error codes to a 404 response code with a 10-second minimum TTL returning /index.html. Furthermore, if a domain name is specified, the template must require a non-empty Route 53 hosted zone ID, automatically creating an ACM certificate in us-east-1 with DNS validation, Route 53 DNS validation records, certificate validation, Route 53 alias A records targeting the distribution, SNI-only SSL support with a default minimum TLS version of TLSv1.2_2021, and optional www. domain aliases with wildcard subject alternative names controlled by a boolean flag defaulting to false.

We need a Terraform template that creates a customizable multi-tier AWS VPC network across 3 active availability zones for hosting production and administrative workloads, defaulting to us-east-1. The VPC must use a base CIDR block constructed as "10.20.0.0/16" with DNS hostnames and DNS support enabled, tagged with default global tags ("Author" = "Fairwinds", "Managed By" = "Terraform"), and connected to an Internet Gateway named "vpc". Across 3 active availability zones (parsed from a comma-separated list of availability zone names, defaulting to a preconfigured set of us-east-1 availability zones), create 4 distinct subnet tiers per availability zone using specific subnet CIDR suffixes appended to the base CIDR: admin subnets (suffixes ".0.0/21", ".8.0/21", ".16.0/21"), public subnets (suffixes ".32.0/21", ".40.0/21", ".48.0/21"), private production subnets (suffixes ".64.0/21", ".72.0/21", ".80.0/21"), and private working subnets (suffixes ".96.0/21", ".104.0/21", ".112.0/21"). Routing must feature one shared public route table associated with all public subnets routing "0.0.0.0/0" to the Internet Gateway, and dedicated per-AZ private route tables (named "private_az1", "private_az2", "private_az3") associated with all admin, private production, and private working subnets. Outbound internet connectivity for private subnets must be supplied via per-AZ Elastic IPs and NAT Gateways deployed into each public subnet (governed by multi_az_nat_gateway set to 1 and single_nat_gateway set to 0), and an S3 Gateway VPC Endpoint must be conditionally provisioned when enable_s3_vpc_endpoint is set to true using a full access policy associated with all private route tables.

We need a Terraform template that creates a self-contained, production-style web backend platform on AWS Fargate, deployed into a new VPC spanning two public and two private subnets across two availability zones in the region, with an internet gateway and separate route tables for the public and private subnets. Traffic should reach the application through an internal Application Load Balancer that drops invalid header fields, with an HTTPS listener on port 443 (self-signed certificate imported into ACM) forwarding to a target group and an HTTP listener on port 80 redirecting to HTTPS, with health checks against a configurable health-check path, backed by an ECS Fargate service split roughly 20 percent on-demand Fargate and 80 percent Fargate Spot capacity, running with a deployment circuit breaker and automatic rollback enabled, and target tracking auto-scaling on both average CPU and memory utilization keeping the service between 2 and 4 running tasks. The task should initially run a placeholder public nginx container image exposing a configurable application port (default 80) that will later be replaced by CI/CD, and it should read its PostgreSQL connection string from environment variables pointing at a companion RDS PostgreSQL database (a small single-AZ instance with encrypted storage is sufficient) placed in the private subnets, using a default username and password of "postgres" for initial bootstrapping and a database named "mydb". A dedicated container registry repository with immutable image tags and scan-on-push should be created for the application image with a lifecycle rule that automatically expires untagged images after 14 days. For CI/CD, set up an IAM OpenID Connect identity provider trusting GitHub Actions' token issuer, with an assumable role restricted to workflows from a given GitHub organization or account (accepted as an input parameter) that is permitted to build and push container images, register new ECS task definitions, pass the task's own IAM roles, update the ECS service, and list, describe, and clean up old task definitions. Configure security groups so that only the load balancer can reach the application containers on any port, only the application containers can reach the database on its PostgreSQL port, the load balancer and the database may only send outbound traffic within the VPC, and the application containers may also only send outbound traffic within the VPC, and create separate ECS execution and task roles, giving the execution role the standard managed ECS task execution permissions needed to pull images and write logs.

We need a Terraform template that creates a self-contained security and identity management foundation for a HashiStack cluster deployment. The module must define input variables for cluster_tag defaulting to "default", enable_key_rotation defaulting to false, and a machine_roles map (mapping role names to sets of policy identifier strings) defaulting to an empty map. Provision a KMS key for Vault unsealing with description "resinstack:vault:seal:{cluster_tag}", annual key rotation set to enable_key_rotation, and a tag "resinstack:cluster" matching cluster_tag. Create seven Secrets Manager secrets tagged with cluster_tag for HashiStack tokens and keys, named "resinstack-{name}-{cluster_tag}" for consul-agent-token, consul-gossip-key, nomad-client-consul-token, nomad-gossip-key, nomad-server-consul-token, nomad-vault-token, and vault-consul-token. Define IAM policies for unsealing Vault via KMS (permitting "kms:Encrypt", "kms:Decrypt", "kms:DescribeKey"), describing EC2 instances ("ResinStackReadTags", permitting "ec2:DescribeInstances"), and retrieving secret values from Secrets Manager tailored for clients (the consul-agent-token, consul-gossip-key, and nomad-client-consul-token secrets), Nomad servers (consul-agent-token, consul-gossip-key, nomad-gossip-key, nomad-server-consul-token, and nomad-vault-token), Consul servers (consul-gossip-key), and Vault servers (consul-gossip-key and vault-consul-token). Dynamically iterate over machine_roles to create EC2 assume roles with a 12-hour maximum session duration and corresponding instance profiles named "resinstack-{role name}-{cluster_tag}", attaching the appropriate IAM policies when their identifiers ("read-tags", "vault-kms", "nomad-keys", "consul-keys", "vault-keys", "client-keys") are present in the role's policy set. Output the Vault KMS key ID, a map of secret names from Secrets Manager, and maps of the generated machine role names and instance profile names.

We need a Terraform template that creates a custom multi-AZ networking foundation for a blog web application. The self-contained stack must deploy a VPC configured with a 64.0.0.0/16 CIDR block, default instance tenancy, DNS support, DNS hostnames, and disabled ClassicLink, tagged with an environment prefix defaulting to "elluis_codes_limited_network". Across a provided map of three availability zones (mapped to subnet offset values 11, 22, and 33), the infrastructure must create public and private subnets that do not auto-assign public IP addresses, using 8-bit CIDR offsets to calculate distinct subnet ranges. Outbound internet connectivity must be enabled via an Internet Gateway attached to the VPC and public route tables routing all traffic out to the Internet Gateway. To support private network egress, allocate an Elastic IP for every availability zone and deploy a NAT Gateway into each corresponding public subnet, connecting them to dedicated per-AZ private route tables that route 0.0.0.0/0 traffic to the NAT Gateways while ignoring future changes to route table and NAT gateway associations.

We need a Terraform template that creates a self-contained Amazon GuardDuty threat detection and findings export infrastructure. The setup must provision a primary GuardDuty detector enabled by default with configurable data sources for S3 logs, Kubernetes audit logs, and EC2 malware scanning, featuring finding publishing frequencies defaulting to "FIFTEEN_MINUTES" and a local-exec provisioner to set EBS snapshot preservation to "RETENTION_WITH_FINDING" or "NO_RETENTION" based on a snapshot retention toggle (defaulting to false). The template must dynamically support custom finding filters, IP sets, threat intelligence sets, and publishing destinations. When IP sets, threat intel sets, or S3 publishing is enabled, the module must automatically provision supporting encryption keys and S3 buckets, including a multi-region KMS key with automated key rotation and a 7-day deletion window, a primary versioned S3 bucket encrypted with the KMS key and configured with server-side access logging to a dedicated log bucket, an IAM replication role and policy, and a secondary replica bucket in a replica region using cross-region provider settings for 15-minute S3 Replication Time Control.

We need a Terraform template that creates the necessary IAM roles and policies for an Amazon EMR cluster, including an EMR service role, an EC2 instance profile role with attached policies for CloudWatch and SSM, an autoscaling role for EMR, and an EC2 instance profile, all parameterized with a name prefix defaulting to "imputation-example" and a tags variable for consistent tagging, and the template should output the ARN, name, and unique ID for each role as well as the instance profile ID, ARN, and name.

We need a Terraform template that creates a dedicated IAM user with programmatic access credentials for API integration testing and monitoring. The stack must deploy an IAM user at root path "/" defaulting in name to "postman-user" along with a set of IAM access keys, attaching policies that grant global read-only access for API Gateway ("apigateway:GET") and CloudWatch metrics ("cloudwatch:GetMetricData", "cloudwatch:ListMetrics"). Additionally, if an optional cognito_user_pool_arn variable (defaulting to an empty string) is supplied, the template must conditionally create and attach an IAM policy granting "cognito-idp:AdminInitiateAuth" permissions specifically scoped to that Cognito user pool ARN.

We need a Terraform template that creates the IAM roles, policies, attachments, and instance profiles required to support an Amazon EKS control plane and worker node group with Cluster Autoscaler integration. The template must declare a cluster_name variable defaulting to "legion" and establish two IAM roles: one named with a "tf-" prefix followed by the cluster name value for the master control plane, and another named with the same prefix followed by the cluster name value and a "-node" suffix for the worker nodes. The master role must allow assume role trust for the EKS service and attach the AWS managed policies "AmazonEKSClusterPolicy" and "AmazonEKSServicePolicy". The worker node role must allow assume role trust for EC2, attach the managed policies "AmazonEKSWorkerNodePolicy", "AmazonEKS_CNI_Policy", and "AmazonEC2ContainerRegistryReadOnly", and be associated with a matching EC2 instance profile whose name follows the same "tf-" prefix, cluster name value, and "-node" suffix pattern. Additionally, the worker node role must be attached to a custom, dynamically-generated IAM policy whose name is prefixed with "eks-worker-autoscaling-" followed by the cluster name value, permitting global describe actions for Auto Scaling groups, Auto Scaling instances, launch configurations, tags, and launch template versions, while restricting capacity modification actions ("autoscaling:SetDesiredCapacity", "autoscaling:TerminateInstanceInAutoScalingGroup", and "autoscaling:UpdateAutoScalingGroup") strictly to resources tagged with a key of "kubernetes.io/cluster/" followed by the cluster name value, equal to "owned", and "k8s.io/cluster-autoscaler/enabled" equal to "true".

We need a Terraform template that creates a self-contained network infrastructure module in AWS to host web server and database workloads. The stack must deploy a VPC defaulting to CIDR block "172.69.0.0/16" tagged "vpc_name", containing a public subnet defaulting to "172.69.1.0/24" tagged "public_subnet" and a private subnet defaulting to "172.69.2.0/24" tagged "private_subnet". Connect the VPC to an internet gateway tagged "igw_tag" and establish a public route table tagged "rtb_tag" that routes "0.0.0.0/0" traffic to the internet gateway and associates directly with the public subnet. Furthermore, provision a web server security group named "webserver-sg_<vpc_id>" tagged "web-server_security_group" supporting dynamic ingress rules (defaulting to TCP port 80 open to "0.0.0.0/0" and port 22 restricted to the VPC CIDR "172.69.0.0/16") with outbound egress limited to the VPC CIDR, alongside a database security group named "database-sg_<vpc_id>" that permits TCP ingress on port 3306.

We need a Terraform template that creates the IAM roles, policies, and instance profiles necessary to support the AWS Cloud Controller Manager and container registry integration for downstream Kubernetes control plane and worker nodes. The module must define a configurable map of tags defaulting to an empty map and create two IAM roles for EC2 assume role access named "aws_ccm_k8s_controlplane" and "aws_ccm_k8s_worker", each associated with a matching EC2 instance profile of the same name. The control plane role must be attached to an IAM policy named "aws_ccm_k8s_controlplane" granting global permissions for EC2 networking, Auto Scaling group description, Elastic Load Balancing management, KMS key description, and service-linked role creation. The worker role must be attached to an IAM policy named "aws_ccm_k8s_worker" granting permissions to describe EC2 instances and regions, along with read-only access to ECR repositories to fetch container images.

We need a Terraform template that creates a foundational IAM security structure with user groups and MFA-enforced administrative roles for multi-user access management. The template must define a configurable name variable defaulting to "awscademo-" to serve as a resource prefix and include default tags for contact, deployment method, deployment date, and infinite TTL. Provision three distinct IAM groups named with the prefix: a demo users group attached to a custom self-management policy allowing users to change their own passwords, manage access keys, upload SSH public keys, and manage virtual MFA devices (including deactivating their own MFA only when MFA is present); a read-only users group attached to the AWS managed ReadOnlyAccess policy; and an MFA superadmin group. Additionally, create an administrative IAM role named with the prefix and truncated to a 31-character name prefix, permitting account root assume-role access with a maximum session duration of 12 hours (43200 seconds), accompanied by an admin policy that grants full administrator permissions conditioned on MFA presence, and attach a group policy to the MFA superadmin group allowing group members to assume this admin role when MFA is present.

We need a Terraform template that creates a self-contained IAM access management infrastructure to support administrative, CI/CD, and serverless deployment workloads. The stack must establish four IAM groups with distinct paths and inline policies: an "admin" group with path "/admin/" granting full wildcard administrative permissions, an "admin-terraform-cloud" group with path "/admin_terraform_cloud/" also granted full wildcard administrative permissions, a "github" group with path "/github/" assigned an inline policy permitting targeted ACM, CloudFront, IAM, Lambda, Route53, S3, and SQS actions, and a "serverless" group with path "/serverless/" assigned a dedicated policy covering ACM, CloudFront, IAM, Lambda, CloudWatch Logs, Route53, S3, and SQS actions. Additionally, the template must provision corresponding IAM users and memberships, specifically "admin" in the admin group, "admin-macbook-pro" in the admin group with an access key, "admin-terraform-cloud" in the admin-terraform-cloud group with an access key, "github" in the github group, and "serverless" in the serverless group. To complete the serverless tooling access, create an IAM role named "serverless" with path "/serverless/" that allows trust assumptions for Lambda and Edge Lambda services, attaching a customer managed policy named "serverless" with path "/serverless/" containing the identical serverless policy permissions.

We need a Terraform template that creates a secure IAM access management framework to enforce multi-factor authentication for user self-management and administrative role assumption. The setup must utilize standardized CloudPosse label modules for consistent naming using namespace, environment, name, tags, and attributes variables across both an admin group and a non-admin group. A self-management policy must be attached to both groups allowing members to manage their own passwords, access keys, virtual MFA devices, and list account MFA devices and password policies, while requiring active MFA specifically to deactivate their virtual MFA devices. The admin group must additionally receive a policy granting permission to assume a dedicated admin role, strictly requiring MFA present for both role assumption and the role's trust policy targeting the account root principal. The admin role must be attached to the AWS-managed AdministratorAccess policy, and both groups must conditionally manage user memberships based on provided lists of admin and non-admin user names.

We need a Terraform template that creates a self-contained multi-tier VPC network stack in AWS across two availability zones for dev/test purposes, using a /16 CIDR block; it must include an internet gateway, one public subnet and two private subnets in each availability zone, where public subnets do not auto-assign public IPs on launch, plus a public route table with a default route to the internet gateway and a private route table with no explicit routes, each associated to its respective subnets, along with a public security group that allows all traffic from the VPC CIDR, SSH from the VPC CIDR, HTTP from anywhere, and outbound traffic only to the VPC CIDR, and a private security group that allows all traffic from the VPC CIDR and outbound traffic only to the VPC CIDR.

We need a Terraform template that creates a complete multi-AZ networking stack for AWS, defaulting to us-east-1, to securely host public web applications and private backend services. The VPC must use a default CIDR block of "10.0.0.0/16" with DNS hostnames and DNS support enabled, tagged with a default vpc_name of "benchmark-vpc" alongside a configurable map of additional tags. Subnets must be dynamically calculated using cidrsubnet functions across all available opt-in availability zones, splitting the CIDR range evenly into matching public subnets (not mapping public IPs on launch) and private subnets. Outbound connectivity requires an Internet Gateway, a dedicated Elastic IP, and a NAT Gateway positioned in the first public subnet. Routing must direct all public subnet traffic to the Internet Gateway, while the private subnets route outbound traffic to the NAT Gateway as the main VPC route table association. The module must manage the default Network ACL and default security group by tagging them with a name combining the VPC name value and the word "Default", while providing custom security groups and explicit Network ACLs for both public and private tiers. Public security group rules must allow HTTP and HTTPS inbound from everywhere, SSH inbound restricted to the CIDR ranges specified in the ssh_inbound list variable (defaulting to ["10.0.0.0/16"]), and HTTP/HTTPS outbound only within the VPC CIDR. Private security group rules must permit HTTP and HTTPS inbound exclusively from the public subnets' CIDRs and HTTPS outbound only within the VPC CIDR. Public NACL rules must allow ingress for HTTP, HTTPS, ephemeral ports (1024-65535), and SSH (using rule numbers starting at 100 for each allowed SSH CIDR), while permitting egress for HTTP, HTTPS, and ephemeral ports. Private NACL rules must allow ingress for HTTP and HTTPS from the public subnets' CIDRs alongside ephemeral ports from everywhere, while permitting egress for HTTPS to everywhere, local ephemeral return traffic to the private subnets, and ephemeral traffic to the public subnets.

We need a Terraform template that creates a multi-tier AWS VPC network infrastructure designed for agentless security scanning workloads across up to 3 available availability zones in the region. The setup must feature a VPC with DNS hostnames and DNS support enabled defaulting to CIDR "10.0.0.0/16" and name tag "DatatogAgentlessScanner", applying default tags for Datadog integration ("Datadog" = "true", "DatadogAgentlessScanner" = "true"). The module must dynamically compute public and offset private subnets across the availability zones, an Internet Gateway with a public route table routing 0.0.0.0/0 to the gateway, a single Elastic IP and NAT Gateway placed in the first public subnet, and a private route table routing 0.0.0.0/0 to the NAT Gateway. Additionally, it must establish private network connectivity via an S3 Gateway VPC Endpoint associated with both route tables, an interface VPC endpoint security group permitting inbound TCP port 443 from the VPC CIDR block, interface VPC endpoints for Lambda and EBS deployed across private subnets with private DNS enabled, and optional SSM interface VPC endpoints for "ec2messages", "ssmmessages", and "ssm" controlled by a boolean flag defaulting to false.

We need a Terraform template that creates a versatile AWS security group management module to manage network access controls for application workloads. The setup must feature a main enable toggle (defaulting to true) and allow toggling between creating a new security group or attaching rules to an existing security group. If a new security group is requested and no VPC ID is supplied, the template must automatically provision a fallback VPC with CIDR 10.0.0.0/16 to host the security group. Resource naming and tagging must integrate with the git-based label module git::https://github.com/sohanyadav/terraform-aws-labels.git?ref=v1.0.0, appending -sg for new security groups and -prefix-list for managed prefix lists. The template must support optional managed prefix list creation when enabled without pre-existing prefix list IDs, defaulting to IPv4 address family and a maximum of 5 entries. Both new and existing security group rule management must support separate categorized rule inputs for ingress and egress based on CIDR blocks, self-referencing rules, source security group IDs, and prefix lists (defaulting to the newly created prefix list when unspecified).

We need a Terraform template that creates a dedicated third-party IAM integration role to enable read-only cost optimization and waste-monitoring analysis via CloudForecast. The IAM role must configure an assume-role trust policy permitting cross-account access from the external principal "arn:aws:iam::656227328603:root" conditioned strictly on matching a customizable external ID variable defaulting to "benchmark-external-id", with the role name controlled by a variable defaulting to "CloudForecast-ZeroWaste". Attached directly to this role, the template must provision fifteen discrete inline IAM policies to grant target read-only describe and list permissions across various AWS services: common metrics and resource tags ("cloudwatch:GetMetricStatistics", "tag:GetResources"), AWS Organizations ("organizations:ListAccounts"), ALB/ELB load balancers and tags, EBS snapshots and volumes, EC2 instances, RDS instances and snapshots, S3 bucket metadata and lifecycle configurations ("s3:ListAllMyBuckets", "s3:ListBucket", "s3:GetBucketLocation", "s3:GetBucketTagging", "s3:GetLifecycleConfiguration"), CloudWatch log group metadata ("logs:DescribeLogGroups"), and Support/Trusted Advisor checks.

We need a Terraform template that creates a set of specialized IAM service users and policies to manage cost reporting, database disaster recovery, data exports, and automated machine image building for a cloud deployment platform. The setup must include a mandatory cost reporting user named with an environment suffix defaulting to "dev" (such as "mattermost-cost-report-dev") attached to an inline policy allowing all Cost Explorer actions across all resources. Additionally, it must support conditional creation toggles for three optional IAM users: a database disaster recovery user with full access to RDS and KMS alongside Secrets Manager access to "rds-cluster-multitenant-*" secret paths, a data exports user with bucket listing and object read/write permissions for a configurable S3 export bucket ARN, and a Packer image builder user with extensive permissions across EC2, Auto Scaling, CloudWatch Events, SSM parameters, IAM profile/role inspections, S3 monitoring state bucket access, specific Lambda function configuration permissions for a "bind-server-network-attachment" function, and pass-role authority for a dedicated server role in the current region and account.

We need a Terraform template that creates the AWS IAM resources, S3 bucket, and ECR repositories required to support Amazon HealthOmics workflows for testing purposes, including the IAM role that the HealthOmics service will assume, a user with programmatic access and a policy allowing pass-role and full omics actions, read-only access to the output bucket and any optional additional S3 buckets, an output bucket for storing results with all public access blocked and SSE-KMS encryption using a customer-managed key, ECR repositories for storing container images with a repository policy allowing the HealthOmics service to pull images, and a role trust policy that allows the omics.amazonaws.com service to assume the role; the AWS region should default to us-east-1, the output bucket should be named "tf-benchmark-omics-output-bucket", the service account user should be named "workbench-health-omics", the IAM role should be named "HealthOmicsRole", the policies for the service and user should be named "HealthOmicsServicePolicy" and "HealthOmicsUserPolicy" respectively, and support should be included for specifying a set of ECR repository names as well as a list of external AWS account IDs to grant cross-account ECR access.

We need a Terraform template that creates a highly available, self-contained Amazon ECS infrastructure and three-AZ network stack to host containerized PaaS applications. The module must default the AWS region to us-east-1, accept a cluster_name variable defaulting to "benchmark", a vpc_cidr_network_octets string defaulting to "10.0", and a default_tags map defaulting to an empty map. Provision an ECS cluster named with a "dit-paas-" prefix, followed by the cluster name value, and a "-cluster" suffix, alongside a VPC configured with a CIDR block formed from the vpc_cidr_network_octets value followed by ".0.0/16", and DNS hostnames disabled. Across the first three availability zones (a, b, and c), configure three public subnets using /22 CIDR allocations formed from the vpc_cidr_network_octets value followed by ".12.0/22", ".16.0/22", and ".20.0/22" respectively, and three private subnets using /22 CIDR allocations formed from the same vpc_cidr_network_octets value followed by ".0.0/22", ".4.0/22", and ".8.0/22" respectively. Internet access must be handled via an Internet Gateway named with the cluster name value followed by "-ig", connected to a shared public route table that directs "0.0.0.0/0" traffic to the gateway for all public subnets. Furthermore, instantiate an Elastic IP and public NAT Gateway in each of the three public subnets, pairing each NAT Gateway with a dedicated private route table for its corresponding private subnet to route outbound "0.0.0.0/0" traffic.

We need a Terraform template that creates a secure, self-contained VPC network module using CloudPosse community modules to host containerized services with private endpoint access. The network stack must deploy a VPC named via a vpc_name variable defaulting to "benchmark-vpc" with primary IPv4 CIDR defaulting to "172.16.0.0/16", enabling DNS hostnames, disabling generated IPv6 CIDRs, and setting default security group rules to deny all traffic. Subnets must be dynamically provisioned across specified availability zones, defaulting to the first three availability zones in the us-east-1 region, enabling NAT gateway support for outbound routing. Furthermore, the configuration must establish an S3 Gateway VPC endpoint associated with the public, private, and default route tables, as well as private DNS-enabled Interface VPC endpoints for ECR Docker, ECR API, CloudWatch Logs, SSM, and KMS residing in the private subnets. Access to these interface endpoints must be controlled by a dedicated security group named "vpc_endpoint_sg" that enforces self-referencing TCP ingress and egress rules exclusively on port 443.

We need a Terraform template that creates a self-contained VPC module with VPC Flow Logs and flexible VPC endpoint support to securely isolate cloud services. The stack must deploy a VPC with configurable name defaulting to "benchmark-vpc", primary CIDR defaulting to "10.0.0.0/16", instance tenancy defaulting to "default", and DNS hostnames enabled by default in region "us-east-1". Enable VPC Flow Logs for ALL traffic, storing logs in a dedicated CloudWatch Log Group named "/aws/vpc-flow-logs/{vpc_name}" with a 180-day retention period, supported by a self-contained IAM role named "vpc_flow_logs_{vpc_name}" and policy granting log stream creation and event delivery. Manage the default VPC security group while provisioning two custom security groups: one named "vpc-endpoints-{vpc_name}" for standard AWS interface endpoints allowing HTTPS port 443 ingress from and egress to specified source security group IDs, and another for custom endpoint services allowing ingress and egress rules mapped specifically to each custom service port and source security group ID combination. Support dynamically created VPC endpoints including Gateway endpoints for "dynamodb" and "s3" attached to provided route tables, private DNS-enabled Interface endpoints for standard AWS services specified in a set defaulting to ["logs"], and non-private DNS Interface endpoints for custom endpoint services defined by key, service name, and port. Finally, if the "ssm" service is included in the requested AWS endpoint services set, automatically provision an IAM role and instance profile both named "ssm_{vpc_name}" with EC2 trust and the "AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore" managed policy attached.

We need a Terraform template that creates a baseline security and encryption-at-rest module establishing account-wide data protection controls. The stack must deploy default EBS encryption enabled at the account level and three separate KMS customer-managed keys with aliases each prefixed "alias/" followed by the project name value and a layer-specific suffix of "-compute", "-observability", or "-storage" for the compute, observability, and storage layers respectively, each with key rotation enabled using a configurable rotation period in days defaulting to 90, a 30-day deletion window, and prevent_destroy lifecycle protection. Configure the compute KMS key policy to permit IAM root access, EC2 service operations for the current account, and Auto Scaling service role usage including grant creation; set the account-level default EBS KMS key to either an optional external key ARN variable or the internal compute KMS key ARN when left blank; configure the observability KMS key policy for IAM root access, CloudWatch Logs conditioned on log group context, CloudTrail, CloudWatch Alarms, SNS, SQS, and EventBridge; and configure the storage KMS key policy for IAM root access, S3 service usage, AWS Config encrypted snapshot delivery, and CloudTrail log encryption. Additionally, enforce account-level public access restrictions by setting EC2 image block public access to "block-new-sharing", EBS snapshot block public access to "block-all-sharing", conditional account-level EC2 instance metadata defaults enforcing required HTTP tokens (IMDSv2) with a configurable hop limit defaulting to 1 when a default-true toggle is set, conditional disabling of EC2 Serial Console access when a default-true toggle is set, and conditional EMR block public access configuration restricting public security groups when a default-true toggle is set.

We need a Terraform template that creates a self-contained, customizable VPC network infrastructure and EC2 inventory node cluster for deployment testing. The module must feature a configurable cluster prefix defaulting to "bench" (restricted to 5-8 characters), a default VPC CIDR of "172.16.0.0/16" with DNS support and DNS hostnames enabled, an Internet Gateway, and a deployment SSH key pair defaulting to "benchmark-keypair" with a valid public key string. The network architecture must dynamically calculate CIDR allocations for user-defined public and private subnet objects across specified availability zones, configuring a default public route table pointing 0.0.0.0/0 to the Internet Gateway and provisioning per-subnet Elastic IPs and public NAT Gateways associated with private route tables for private subnets. Security group rules must establish a default security group supporting full self-referencing intra-group ingress, outbound traffic only within the VPC CIDR, and custom dynamic ingress CIDR rules. For compute nodes defined via an inventory node list, the setup must retrieve recent AMIs, provision EBS-optimized EC2 instances attached to subnets via index positioning with configurable root volumes and optional Elastic IPs, and construct attached secondary EBS volumes mapped to specified device names and mount points.

We need a Terraform template that creates a versatile VPC networking module named "benchmark-vpc" defaulting to the us-east-1 region with a CIDR block of "10.0.0.0/16", an Internet Gateway, a default security group allowing only self-referencing ingress and egress, an additional security group allowing inbound TLS traffic on port 443, and flexible public or private subnet layouts using specific default subnet CIDR allocations ("10.0.1.0/24", "10.0.2.0/24", "10.0.3.0/24", and "10.0.4.0/24"). When private subnets are enabled via a boolean toggle defaulting to true, the template must provision two public subnets in the first two availability zones and two private subnets in those same availability zones using the third and fourth CIDR blocks, while toggling private subnets to false must instead create four public subnets across four availability zones. Furthermore, the private routing infrastructure must support mutually exclusive egress routing strategies controlled by independent boolean toggles: deploying redundant NAT Gateways in each public subnet with associated Elastic IPs and private route tables, deploying redundant NAT EC2 instances (m1.small) using Amazon Linux NAT AMIs in each public subnet with custom security group rules and private route tables pointing to their primary network interfaces, or creating an Egress-Only Internet Gateway with IPv6 egress routes to ::/0.

We need a Terraform template that creates a self-contained multi-region S3 infrastructure for managing Terraform state and access logs, with cross-region replication for disaster recovery. The template should provision two S3 buckets in the primary AWS region (defaulting to us-east-1): one for Terraform state files and one for access logs. The state bucket must have server-side encryption using AWS KMS, versioning enabled, and logging configured to send access logs to the access logs bucket. The access logs bucket should have versioning enabled, a lifecycle rule that transitions objects to Glacier after a configurable number of days (default 7) and expires them after another configurable number of days (default 30), and an ACL set to log-delivery-write. We need a Terraform template that creates a versatile VPC networking and private interface endpoint module supporting either new VPC provisioning or integration with existing infrastructure. The stack must deploy a VPC named via a name variable defaulting to "benchmark-vpc" with primary CIDR "10.0.0.0/16", enabling DNS hostnames and DNS support by default in us-east-1, unless an existing vpc_id is supplied. Unless overridden by pre-existing subnet ID maps, the module must provision public subnets (not mapping public IPs on launch by default), private subnets, and database subnets using a default CIDR map across two default availability zones in the us-east-1 region, alongside an RDS database subnet group named using a lowercased version of the VPC name. We need a Terraform template that creates an isolated testing VPC environment to validate AWS Systems Manager Session Manager connectivity for EC2 instances without internet access. Configure a test EC2 instance of type t3.small using the latest Amazon Linux 2 x86_64 EBS-backed AMI running in the private subnet with IMDSv2 required, an encrypted root volume, and source/destination checks disabled and attached to an instance security group that allows egress port 443 TCP traffic restricted to the VPC CIDR with no ingress rules. Provide an IAM instance profile and role with permissions for SSM, SSMMessages, EC2Messages, CloudWatch Logs, KMS data key generation, and S3 object actions, ensuring both the IAM role and instance profile names use prefixes based on an application shortcode variable defaulting to "bmk".

We need a Terraform template that creates a secure, private ECS Fargate deployment to run an NGINX service alongside an SSM-managed jumphost for internal testing in us-east-1. The infrastructure must include a VPC with a /16 CIDR block spanning three Availability Zones, featuring three public and three private subnets, one NAT gateway per Availability Zone, and enabled DNS hostnames. Deploy this as a Fargate service with a desired count of 1 task in the private subnets, assign dedicated execution and task IAM roles with necessary inline policies for ECR pulls, logging, parameter access, and service discovery, secure it with a task security group allowing port 80 ingress from the VPC, and register it to the Cloud Map namespace with multivalue A and SRV records using a 10-second TTL and a custom health check failure threshold of 1. To facilitate testing, launch a t3.micro Amazon Linux 2 EC2 instance in the first public subnet using a custom network interface with a static private IP, attach an IAM instance profile with the AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore managed policy, and secure it with a security group allowing all inbound traffic from the VPC. Finally, provide a Terraform output containing the exact curl command required to reach the NGINX service via its private service discovery DNS name.

We need a Terraform template that creates a complete benchmark environment in us-east-1 centered around a t3.micro Amazon Linux 2 EC2 instance and its supporting networking and identity infrastructure. We need a Terraform template that creates a custom Amazon EKS cluster named "demo-eks" with unmanaged worker nodes deployed via a CloudFormation-managed Auto Scaling Group in a new VPC across three availability zones in us-east-1, ensuring the AWS provider applies a default tag of "kubernetes.io/cluster/demo-eks" set to "owned". Next, configure an EC2 launch template using a t3.medium instance, a 30 GB gp2 root volume, required IMDSv2 HTTP tokens with a hop limit of 2, the latest Amazon Linux 2 EKS-optimized AMI retrieved via SSM, and a base64-encoded user-data bootstrap script that connects to the cluster and signals a CloudFormation stack upon completion. After incorporating a 30-second delay to allow the launch template to settle, deploy a CloudFormation stack named "eks-cluster-stack" to provision the Auto Scaling Group across the private subnets with a minimum size of 1, desired capacity of 3, and maximum size of 4, ensuring it incorporates an update policy for rolling updates with a maximum batch size of 1, a minimum of 3 instances in service, and a 5-minute pause time. We need a Terraform template that creates a secure, highly durable remote state management architecture for multiple EKS stacks, utilizing an S3 backend in us-east-1 with cross-region replication to a second AWS region. The deployment must provision a primary S3 bucket named dynamically with the AWS account ID, enforcing versioning, strict public access blocks, and a bucket policy that explicitly denies non-SSL requests. Configure S3 cross-region replication on the primary bucket to automatically replicate KMS-encrypted objects to the replica bucket, attaching an IAM role with the precise permissions required to read the source objects, decrypt them using the primary KMS key, and encrypt them at the destination using the replica key. To support concurrent operations, iterate through a provided map of stack names and regions to deploy individual pay-per-request DynamoDB tables keyed by "LockID" for each stack's state locking, alongside dedicated IAM policies that grant stack-specific access to their respective DynamoDB table, S3 bucket prefix, and KMS key operations. Finally, the template must automatically generate a local "backend.tf" file for each stack within a relative "eks-stacks" directory to seamlessly integrate these backend configurations into our workflows, ensuring all created resources are tagged with a standardized set of state management labels.

We need a Terraform template that creates a WebSocket API on Amazon API Gateway v2 that forwards client messages directly into an Amazon SQS queue without any Lambda functions. Use a randomly generated two-word pet name for both the API and the queue, encrypt the queue with a dedicated customer-managed KMS key with automatic rotation, and create an IAM execution role assumable by API Gateway with SQS access and CloudWatch Logs permissions. Deploy the API to an auto-deployed stage named "dev" with access logging to a CloudWatch log group under the /aws/apigateway/ prefix retained for one day, and output the full WebSocket endpoint URL including the stage name.

We need a Terraform template that creates five standalone VPCs for network testing, each with default instance tenancy and DNS support enabled: a VPC named "XXXX-vpc-test" with CIDR 10.0.0.0/16; a VPC named "Default" with CIDR 172.31.0.0/16 and DNS hostnames enabled; a VPC named "eksctl-eks-cluster-px-cluster/VPC" with CIDR 192.168.0.0/16 and DNS hostnames enabled, carrying eksctl tags that record the cluster name "eks-cluster-px" and eksctl version "0.94.0"; an untagged VPC with CIDR 10.0.0.0/24; and a VPC with CIDR 10.0.0.0/16 and an empty Name tag, with all CIDR, tag, and DNS values exposed as variables with these defaults.

We need a Terraform template that creates the IAM roles needed to run scheduled ECS tasks: an ECS service role named "ecs-role" trusted by ecs.amazonaws.com with the AWS managed AmazonEC2ContainerServiceRole policy attached, an ECS task execution role named "ecs-tasks-role" trusted by ecs-tasks.amazonaws.com with the AWS managed AmazonECSTaskExecutionRolePolicy attached, and an EventBridge role named "events-role" trusted by events.amazonaws.com. We need a Terraform template that creates an Amazon S3 Multi-Region Access Point backed by two replicated buckets for highly available object storage. Finally, create a Multi-Region Access Point named from a variable defaulting to "example-mrap" spanning both buckets, with an access point policy that allows only the owning account to get and put objects through it.

We need a Terraform template that creates an AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager setup that scans and patches EC2 instances on a weekly schedule, using Cloud Posse null-label naming conventions for resource names and tags. Provision two maintenance windows, a scan window scheduled by default at cron(0 0 18 ? * WED *) and an install window scheduled by default at cron(0 0 21 ? * WED *), each lasting 3 hours with a 1-hour cutoff. Each window needs an instance target, defaulting to instances tagged with Patch Group "TOSCAN" for scanning and "TOPATCH" for installing unless explicit tag targets are provided, and a Run Command task using the AWS-RunPatchBaseline document with a maximum concurrency of 20 and maximum errors of 50, where the scan task runs the Scan operation without rebooting and the install task runs the Install operation with a reboot option defaulting to RebootIfNeeded. Also create an AMAZON_LINUX_2 patch baseline with a HIGH compliance level for approved patches and a default approval rule that automatically approves Critical, Important, and Medium severity Security, Bugfix, and Recommended patches for Amazon Linux 2 after 7 days with non-security updates enabled, and register both patch groups against that baseline.

We need a Terraform template that creates an account activity monitoring stack that alerts on sensitive management changes. It must create a multi-region CloudTrail trail named "monitor_account_activities" with global service events and log file validation enabled, recording all management events except those from KMS and RDS Data, encrypted with a dedicated customer-managed KMS key with automatic rotation. In the "management_activities" metric namespace, create CloudWatch Logs metric filters with matching alarms for security group changes, IAM user creation or deletion, failed console logins, IAM group, role, and user policy changes, IAM policy changes, users being added to groups, and IAM role creation or deletion, where each alarm fires when the metric reaches 1 or more within a 60-second period. Every alarm must notify an SNS topic named "management-updates" that is encrypted with its own rotating customer-managed KMS key allowing CloudWatch to publish, with email subscriptions for a configurable list of recipients defaulting to a single placeholder address.

We need a Terraform template that creates a secure static frontend hosting stack together with a Terraform remote state backend. The frontend uses a private S3 bucket named "s3-frontend-nft-maker-v2" suffixed with the account ID, blocking all public access, encrypted with SSE-KMS using a dedicated customer-managed KMS key with automatic rotation, configured for website hosting with "index.html" as both the index and error document, and with a CORS rule allowing GET, PUT, POST, and DELETE from any origin. We need a Terraform template that creates a Kubernetes-ready, dual-stack VPC network foundation for an EKS cluster named "stackx" spread across three availability zones in the region. Optional database, cache, and internal (no internet) subnet tiers with their own route tables and RDS or ElastiCache subnet groups should be supported but disabled by default.

We need a Terraform template that creates a scheduled weather-data lake pipeline built on AWS Glue and Step Functions. We need a Terraform template that creates a basic CI/CD pipeline for a static website served through CloudFront, defaulting to us-east-1. We need a Terraform template that creates a reusable, general-purpose VPC module for AWS in us-east-1 that, with its default settings, provisions a single VPC named "main" with the CIDR block 10.0.0.0/16, default instance tenancy, DNS support enabled, DNS hostnames disabled, and no IPv6 CIDR block. We need a Terraform template that creates a basic team-based IAM access structure with three groups, "BillingGroup", "AdminGroup", and "SuportGroup", each with a matching user named "Billing", "Admin", and "Suport" who is a member of that group and has a console login profile with an 8-character generated password. We need a Terraform template that creates an encrypted Amazon EFS file system for shared storage testing, using the general purpose performance mode and bursting throughput mode with a Terraform-generated creation token and the default AWS-managed encryption key, and attaches a backup policy with automatic backups enabled. We need a Terraform template that creates the foundational state storage and service IAM roles for an NLP data pipeline built on AWS Glue, Amazon Comprehend, Lambda, and Step Functions. We need a Terraform template that creates a minimal AWS stack for a ZenML machine learning pipeline. It should create an S3 artifact store bucket named "demo-artifact-store" followed by the current AWS account ID, with force destroy enabled, bucket-owner-preferred object ownership, a private ACL, all public access blocked, and default SSE-KMS encryption using a new customer-managed KMS key with rotation enabled. It should also create an ECR repository named "zenml-kubernetes" with immutable image tags and scan on push enabled, tag resources with managedBy "terraform" and application "demo", and write a local ZenML stack YAML file for ZenML version "0.12.0" that references the artifact bucket path, the account's ECR registry URI, and AWS Secrets Manager as the secrets manager.

We need a Terraform template that creates an IAM task execution role for Amazon ECS tasks, trusted by the ECS tasks service and named from the prefix "nim" with an "-ecs_task_execution-" suffix, with the AWS-managed AmazonECSTaskExecutionRolePolicy attached. We need a Terraform template that creates an AWS Organization with all features enabled and the AI services opt-out, backup, service control, and tag policy types enabled on the organization root, with support for optionally defining a nested hierarchy of organizational units up to five levels deep from a list of slash-delimited paths, which defaults to empty so no organizational units are created.

We need a Terraform template that creates a VPC named "swe-vpc" with CIDR block 10.0.0.0/16, default instance tenancy, and DNS support and DNS hostnames enabled, tagged with a ResourceGroup tag of "default". The stack should take over the VPC's default network ACL, naming it "swe-vpc-default_acl", so that it allows all traffic to and from the VPC's own CIDR and explicitly denies inbound SSH (port 22) and RDP (port 3389) from any external address.
