We need a Terraform template that creates two separate VPCs for development and recette (staging) environments: "vpc_dev" with CIDR 10.16.0.0/16 and "vpc_rec" with CIDR 10.32.0.0/16. Each VPC should contain six subnets split evenly across the first two availability zones in the region, organized as a public pair (x.12.0/24 in the first zone and x.11.0/24 in the second), an internal pair (x.1.0/24 and x.2.0/24), and an external pair (x.5.0/24 and x.6.0/24), where x is 10.16 for dev and 10.32 for rec, with subnet names following the pattern "subnet_dev_public_a" and "subnet_rec_internal_b". Attach an internet gateway named "gatway_dev" or "gatway_rec" to each VPC and add a default internet route (IPv4 and IPv6) through that gateway on each VPC's main route table, and output both VPC IDs.

We need a Terraform template that creates and enables an Amazon GuardDuty detector for the account in us-east-1, with S3 protection turned off and the finding publishing frequency left at the service default, using Cloud Posse label conventions for naming. Optional EventBridge rules and SNS topic notifications for findings should be supported but disabled by default, so no topic, topic policy, or event rule is created.

We need a Terraform template that creates an AWS Backup configuration whose resource names are all prefixed with "sudo-backup-" followed by a random six-character lowercase alphanumeric string. The stack should create a customer-managed KMS key with key rotation enabled and use it to encrypt a backup vault named "<prefix>-backup-vault". Create a backup plan named "<prefix>-backup-plan" with a single rule named "<prefix>-backup-rule" that targets that vault on the daily schedule "cron(0 12 * * ? *)" (noon UTC), tags recovery points with a Name tag, and by default has no lifecycle transition or expiration and no cross-vault copy action. Create an IAM role named "<prefix>-backup-role" that AWS Backup can assume, attach the AWS managed backup service role policy to it, and add a backup selection named "<prefix>-backup-selection" that uses this role to back up resources tagged with key "backup" equal to "true".

We need a Terraform template that creates Amazon Cognito authentication for an application named "coop-tweets". It should create a user pool named "coop-tweets" where only administrators can create users and passwords must be at least 6 characters long and include numbers, uppercase letters, and symbols, plus a hosted user pool domain with the prefix "coop-tweets-domain". It should also create an identity pool named "coop tweets" that does not allow unauthenticated identities, and attach two IAM roles to it, "coop-tweets_cognito_auth_role" for authenticated identities and "coop-tweets_cognito_unauth_role" for unauthenticated identities, each trusting Cognito federated identities for this identity pool only and each granted a customer-managed policy ("cognito_kibana_auth_coop-tweets" and "cognito_kibana_unauth_coop-tweets") allowing mobile analytics events and Cognito Sync and Cognito Identity actions.

We need a Terraform template that creates an enabled Amazon GuardDuty detector that publishes findings every fifteen minutes, together with a customer-managed KMS key with automatic rotation and a 30-day deletion window, aliased "alias/guardduty", whose key policy grants the account full administration and allows the GuardDuty service to generate data keys for encrypting findings exports. Also create an EventBridge rule named "guardduty-finding-events" that matches GuardDuty Finding events; exporting findings to an S3 bucket should be optional and disabled by default.

We need a Terraform template that creates a private Amazon S3 bucket with an auto-generated name that can be force-destroyed, with all four public access block settings enabled, versioning enabled with MFA delete disabled, default server-side encryption using S3-managed keys (AES256) with bucket keys enabled, object ownership set to "BucketOwnerPreferred", and a private canned ACL applied after the ownership controls are in place.

We need a Terraform template that creates IAM roles and groups for delegating access to the AWS billing console within the current account. Create two roles, "billing-full-access" and "billing-view-access", each assumable by principals in the current account only when MFA is present: the full-access role gets a customer-managed policy named "billing-full-access" allowing all billing, usage, payment-method, and budget management actions, while the view-access role gets a customer-managed policy named "billing-view-access" allowing only viewing of billing, usage, account, payment methods, and budgets. Also create two IAM groups at path "/", "billing-full-access" and "billing-view-access", each with an attached policy (named "billing-full-access-assume-role" and "billing-view-access-assume-role" respectively) that allows members to assume the matching role; group user memberships are configurable but empty by default, so no memberships are created. Output the ARNs of both roles and both groups.

We need a Terraform template that creates an Amazon Cognito identity setup for application users, with all resources named from a base name of "cognito" plus a randomly generated pet-name suffix. It should create a user pool (hyphens in the name replaced by underscores) with MFA turned off, email as an auto-verified attribute, a custom profile schema consisting of a required immutable email attribute, an optional immutable phone number attribute, and mutable string attributes for profile user ID, email, first name, last name, gender, age, and persona, and SMS sending enabled through an IAM role that Cognito can assume with a random 16-character uppercase external ID and a policy allowing it to publish to SNS. Add a user pool app client without a client secret, and an identity pool that allows unauthenticated identities and uses the user pool client as its identity provider. Attach two roles to the identity pool, a signed-users role for authenticated identities and an anonymous-users role for unauthenticated identities, both trusting Cognito federated identities for this pool only; grant the authenticated role Cognito Identity and Cognito Sync permissions scoped to this identity pool, and the unauthenticated role Cognito Identity permissions only, while also looking up the current partition, region, and account through a helper module.

We need a Terraform template that creates an AWS Batch environment for running pipeline tasks, with every resource named after the Terraform workspace plus a "-batch" suffix (for example "default-batch") and tagged accordingly. The network should be a new VPC with CIDR 192.168.0.0/16 containing a private subnet 192.168.0.0/24 and a public subnet 192.168.10.0/24, both in the second availability zone of the region, with an internet gateway for the public subnet and a NAT gateway with an Elastic IP in the public subnet that provides outbound access for the private subnet; neither subnet auto-assigns public IPs. Create a managed, enabled EC2 compute environment in the private subnet using the best-fit allocation strategy, "optimal" instance types, the AWS-managed Amazon Linux 2023 ECS-optimized image, 0 minimum and 4 maximum vCPUs, and a security group whose only egress rule allows HTTPS to the VPC CIDR, plus an enabled job queue named with a "-queue" suffix at priority 1. Store results in an S3 bucket named "benchmark-batch-results" suffixed with the account ID, blocking all public access and encrypted with a new customer-managed KMS key with rotation. The ECS instance role and instance profile should carry the AWS-managed ECS-for-EC2 policy and a custom "ecs_s3_policy" granting read/list on S3 generally, read/write/delete on the results bucket, and decrypt/generate-data-key on the bucket key; also create a Batch service role with the AWS-managed Batch service policy.

We need a Terraform template that creates a secure S3 bucket for endpoint backups named "endpoint-backup" followed by a hyphen and the current AWS account ID, with all public access blocked, transfer acceleration suspended, object lock disabled, and default server-side encryption using S3-managed keys (AES256). Attach a bucket policy that denies insecure requests not made over TLS 1.2 or higher and denies uploads or retention changes that would place objects in compliance-mode lock for more than 90 days. Also create an IAM user named "endpoint-backup" and a customer-managed IAM policy named "endpoint-backup-bucket-read-write-access" granting list, read, write, delete, version, retention, and restore access to this bucket and decrypt/data-key access on the AWS-managed S3 KMS key, attached to that user, without creating any access keys.

We need a Terraform template that creates a shared-services Amazon Cognito user pool named "unity-shared-services-user-pool" in which only administrators can create users, account recovery uses verified email, and the invitation email and SMS messages are customized to deliver the username and temporary password. The pool's ID should be published to a String SSM parameter named "/unity/cs/security/shared-services-cognito-user-pool/user-pool-id", and the pool should get a hosted UI domain with the prefix "unity-shared-services-test". Register six app clients against the pool, named "unity-uds-distribution-user-pool-client", "localhost-jupyterhub-user-pool-client", "unity-app-to-app-client-user-pool-client", "uads-jupyter-development-client-user-pool-client", "hysds-ui-client-user-pool-client", and "localhost-hysds-ui-client-user-pool-client", each using the authorization code OAuth flow with the email and openid scopes and the Cognito identity provider, with callback and logout URLs supplied as variables that default to sample API endpoints or local development addresses. The first four clients should generate a client secret while the two HySDS UI clients should not, and the app-to-app and development Jupyter clients should not allow username/password authentication. Finally, create two user groups in the pool, "Unity_Admin" and "Unity_Viewer".

We need a Terraform template that creates a reusable application VPC in us-east-1 named "vpc-terraform-testing" (app name "terraform", environment "testing") with CIDR 10.0.0.0/16, DNS hostnames disabled, and IPv6 off by default. Spread it across three availability zones in the region, with one public and one private subnet per zone using the public CIDRs 10.0.10.0/24, 10.0.20.0/24, and 10.0.30.0/24 and the private CIDRs 10.0.11.0/24, 10.0.22.0/24, and 10.0.33.0/24, tagging subnets and other resources with the app name and environment. Attach an internet gateway with a public route table that sends internet traffic from the public subnets through it, and create an Elastic IP and a single NAT gateway in the first public subnet so that a shared private route table sends the private subnets' outbound traffic through the NAT. Finally, create a DB subnet group named "db-subnet-terraform-testing" spanning the private subnets and output the VPC, subnet, default security group, and NAT gateway details; transit gateway attachment and IPv6 egress routing should be optional and disabled by default.

We need a Terraform template that creates three AWS CodeCommit repositories for an Argo CD GitOps bridge, named "gitops-apps", "gitops-platform", and "gitops-addons", along with an IAM user named "gitops-bridge-gitops" that authenticates over SSH using a newly generated 4096-bit RSA key pair uploaded as the user's SSH public key. Grant that user Git pull and push access to only these three repositories through a customer-managed IAM policy named "gitops-bridge-gitops", store the generated private key in a Secrets Manager secret whose name starts with "codecommit-key-" followed by a random five-character suffix, write the private key locally as "gitops_ssh.pem" in the user's SSH directory, and add a matching SSH config entry for the CodeCommit Git endpoints.

We need a Terraform template that creates a reusable single EC2 instance module in us-east-1 which, with its default settings, also builds its own network: a VPC with the CIDR block 10.70.0.0/16 and DNS support and hostnames enabled, one subnet 10.70.0.0/24 in the first available availability zone that does not auto-assign public IPs, and an internet gateway with a route table sending default traffic to it. Launch a t2.micro instance named "benchmark-instance" from the latest Ubuntu 22.04 AMI in that subnet with detailed monitoring enabled, a public IP address, an encrypted 10 GiB gp2 root volume, IMDSv2 required, and an SSH key pair named "benchmark-d8bc612be4e0-key" that the template creates from a supplied public key, and attach an Elastic IP to it. Give the instance an IAM role and instance profile that EC2 can assume, plus a dedicated security group whose only rule allows egress to the VPC's own CIDR block, with no ingress ports opened by default. Finally, add a CloudWatch alarm on the instance's StatusCheckFailed_Instance metric (maximum over 60-second periods, alarming when it is at least 1 for 5 consecutive periods) whose action automatically reboots the instance. Optional extra EBS volumes and additional network interfaces with Elastic IPs should be supported but not created by default.

We need a Terraform template that creates a cross-region S3 replication setup for log buckets tagged with Env "dev", spanning four regions: two source regions (the first being us-east-1) and two separate replica regions. In the primary source region, create two source buckets named "log1a.veerum" and "log1b.veerum", and in the second source region two source buckets named "log2a.veerum" and "log2b.veerum", each followed by a hyphen and the current AWS account ID. In each replica region, create four replica buckets, one per source bucket, named after the source bucket with a "-replica1" or "-replica2" suffix respectively followed by the account ID. Every bucket must be private with versioning enabled, block all public access, and use default SSE-KMS encryption with a customer-managed KMS key created in its own region, aliased "alias/sourcekey1", "alias/sourcekey2", "alias/replicakey1", and "alias/replicakey2". Each source bucket needs two enabled replication rules covering all objects, including SSE-KMS encrypted objects, that copy them in the STANDARD storage class to its matching replica bucket in each replica region, re-encrypting with that region's replica key. Replication should run under an IAM role that S3 can assume, with a customer-managed policy allowing it to read the source buckets and object versions, replicate objects and deletes into the replica buckets, decrypt with the source keys, and encrypt with the replica keys.

We need a Terraform template that creates an enabled Amazon GuardDuty detector that publishes findings every fifteen minutes and is tagged with the module's repository URL. Enable the S3 data events, RDS login events, Lambda network logs, EKS audit logs, and EBS malware protection detector features, and turn on runtime monitoring for EKS, ECS Fargate, and EC2 while leaving GuardDuty's automatic agent management for each of those disabled. After the detector is created, run an AWS CLI command that configures malware scan settings so EBS snapshots are not retained. The template should also support, but not create by default, findings filters, trusted IP sets, threat intelligence sets, a malware protection plan for S3 buckets, and exporting findings to a versioned, access-logged, KMS-encrypted and cross-region-replicated S3 bucket; with the default settings none of those buckets, KMS keys, or replication roles are created.
